quest:1007.text: The Ancient Statuette. Talen, an elf camped near the dangerous Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale, seeks recovery of a lost relic. After being ambushed and run aground by vicious naga, he dropped his prized ancient statuette along the surf and needs an adventurer to retrieve it from the ruins. The sunken ruins of Zoram along Ashenvale's northwestern shoreline have long attracted those curious about the ancient night elven past. Talen was navigating the shallows in a small vessel when hostile naga surfaced and tore into him with claw and trident. He managed to scramble ashore with bare provisions to make a hasty camp, but in his desperate sprint for survival, his most precious find was dropped into the sands. The ancient statuette left half-buried on the beach is more than a simple souvenir. Talen considers it the entire justification for braving the monster-infested Zoram Strand. Upon its recovery, he reveals that the drowned city holds centuries of forgotten mysteries, and this delicate carving acts as a vital key to understanding what remains hidden beneath the tides.

quest:1010.text: Bathran's Hair. Bathran's Hair is an Alliance quest offered by Orendil Broadleaf at Maestra's Post in western Ashenvale. Desperate to treat a mysteriously afflicted night elf child whose illness transcends the physical body, Orendil sends adventurers north to scour the ancient ruins of Bathran's Haunt for a restorative plant renowned for mending ailments of the spirit. At Maestra's Post, just south of the Darkshore border, the night elf herbalist Orendil Broadleaf faces a troubling medical crisis. A young child in Astranaar has fallen grievously ill, exhibiting symptoms that resist ordinary physical remedies. Convinced that the sickness plagues the child's spirit rather than merely the flesh, Orendil seeks Bathran's Hair, an uncommon restorative herb historically gathered amidst the ancient elven ruins to the north.

quest:1023.text: Raene's Cleansing. This quest marks the tragic continuation of the search for Teronis, a night elf sentinel sent to Lake Falathim. Upon discovering his remains on the shore, the task shifts to recovering his research journal and retrieving the glowing gem held by local murlocs before reporting the grim news back to Astranaar. Sent to Lake Falathim by Raene Wolfrunner, adventurers discover Teronis dead along the waterside. Rather than a rescue, the mission turns into salvage and investigation. Among his belongings lies an intact journal detailing his assignment and findings regarding the strange disturbances in Ashenvale. Teronis had tracked a rare, luminous stone to the lake, which fell into the possession of the aggressive murlocs infesting the shallows. Recovering both Teronis' journal and pryed-away gem is necessary to carry forward the late scout's original mission.

quest:1024.text: Raene's Cleansing. This intermediate step in the investigation of Ashenvale's corruption sends Alliance adventurers deep into the sacred groves east of Iris Lake. Entrusted with a recovered Glowing Gem, you must consult the dryad Shael'dryn to learn how to restore Dartol's ancient rod. Following the tragic death of the sentinel Teronis, Raene Wolfrunner examines the field notes he left behind. His research indicates that investigating Ashenvale's troubled furbolgs may require an ancient artifact: a rod crafted long ago by a night elf named Dartol. With only a Glowing Gem in hand, Raene admits her tactical expertise as a huntress is ill-suited to deciphering lost arcane and natural mysteries. Rather than guessing at the remaining pieces of Dartol's Rod, Raene directs travelers northeast toward Iris Lake. Tucked away beside a tranquil moonwell dwells Shael'dryn, a dryad whose natural communion with the forest grants her deep insight into ancient relics. By delivering the gem to her, adventurers hope to uncover the missing components and learn how to reforge the rod.

quest:104.text: The Coastal Menace. Captain Grayson's restless ghost watches the rocky coast of Westfall, haunted by the memory of the shipwreck that took his life and the slaughter of the lighthouse keeper's family. He charges travelers with hunting down the vicious murloc chieftain responsible: Old Murk-Eye. Slaying the beast brings a measure of justice to the shore and helps safeguard future sailors. The Westfall Lighthouse stands as the lone guide through the jagged shallows of the southern coast, but its flame has flickered through bloody tragedies. Captain Grayson lost his life when his vessel broke against the rocks in the dark, an accident precipitated when murlocs terrified the lighthouse keeper's family into fleeing their post. Though the family later returned and relit the flame, the reprieve was brief. The shoreline remained stalked by a particularly cunning and ruthless predator. Old Murk-Eye is not merely another wild beast prowling the tide pools. Grayson recounts watching the creature sway the weaker-minded murlocs along the coast, rallying them into a coordinated strike against the lighthouse. The second raid proved fatal, wiping out the keeper's family before Grayson's helpless spectral eyes. To bring peace to the dead and preserve what remains of safety on the Great Sea, the ghostly captain demands Murk-Eye's death and a scale as proof.

quest:1060.text: Letter to Jin'Zil. Letter to Jin'Zil is a Horde delivery quest entrusted to adventurers who have slain Serena Bloodfeather in the northern Barrens. Orc rogue Darsok Swiftdagger sends you across the border into the rugged crags of Stonetalon Mountains to deliver word of the harpy matriarch's demise to his old friend, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil. After the harpy threat around the northern Barrens is systematically dismantled, Darsok Swiftdagger reveals that the winged raiders were never native to the scrublands. The Witchwing and Bloodfeather broods descended from the rugged ridges of the Stonetalon Mountains to the northwest. Impressed by your prowess in dispatching Serena Bloodfeather, Darsok sends you into those dangerous peaks to carry news of her death to an old acquaintance, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil, residing at the troll settlement of Malaka'jin.

quest:1069.text: Deepmoss Spider Eggs. Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet aims to capitalize on an exotic culinary craze sweeping Booty Bay: spider egg omelettes. To supply the lucrative overseas market, he hires adventurers to venture into the Stonetalon Mountains and harvest fresh clutches of deepmoss spider eggs. Booty Bay's high rollers and eccentric pirates have developed an insatiable appetite for spider egg omelettes, sparking high demand for rare ingredients across the Great Sea. Recognizing an easy fortune, Ratchet merchant Mebok Mizzyrix has jumped at the chance to supply the southern port. Because the Eastern Kingdoms lack this particular arachnid delicacies, Kalimdor's rugged wilderness provides the perfect supply chain. The harvest requires trekking into the Stonetalon Mountains to find deepmoss spiders. Clutches of their eggs can be discovered clinging beneath the surviving timber of the Venture Company's logging operations in Windshear Crag, or deeper within the web-strewn depths of Sishir Canyon. Gathering the eggs means risking venomous bites and confronting dense infestations that make even seasoned scavengers squeamish. Speed and logistics are critical when moving raw arachnid eggs across the sea before they spoil or hatch. Mebok coordinates closely with Ratchet's Wharfmaster Dizzywig, arranging freight passage on goblin merchant ships bound straight for the docks of Stranglethorn Vale. With the eggs safely packed in crates, Mebok turns a tidy profit on high-seas gastronomy.

quest:1070.text: On Guard in Stonetalon. On Guard in Stonetalon is an Alliance breadcrumb quest directing adventurers south from Ashenvale into the rugged Stonetalon Mountains. Sentinel Thenysil dispatches travelers to check on her scout friend, Kaela Shadowspear, who was sent into the crags alongside a gnome mage to monitor industrial incursions by the Venture Company. Stationed in Astranaar, Sentinel Thenysil keeps a close watch on threats pressing toward the ancient forest. Deeply concerned for her friend Kaela Shadowspear, Thenysil asks passing Alliance champions to track her down. Kaela was dispatched into the Stonetalon Mountains by Sentinel Wolfrunner to survey rising turmoil in the heights, but communication has fallen silent, leaving Thenysil anxious for her safety. Thenysil's concern is heightened by Kaela's assigned companion: a gnome mage deployed alongside her by the Alliance leadership. While the night elves have joined the Grand Alliance out of strategic necessity, many Sentinels remain deeply skeptical of arcane practitioners and tinkering gnomes operating in pristine wilderness. Finding Kaela perched on the bluffs above Windshear Crag reveals an outpost keeping vigil over widespread environmental devastation wrought by the Venture Company.

quest:1071.text: A Gnome's Respite. A Gnome's Respite is an Alliance quest offered by the eccentric tinkerer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. Overwhelmed by the Venture Company's rapid industrial push into Windshear Crag, Gaxim hires adventurers to cull their loggers and deforesters so he can buy enough breathing room to invent new deterrents. Gaxim Rustfizzle represents the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences. Stationed among the ancient groves of Stonetalon, his stated duty is proving to the nature-worshipping night elves that modern gnomish invention—blending magic, chemical brews, and mechanics—can actively protect their threatened lands. However, the relentless pace of the Venture Company has left him with barely any time to prototype his defensive devices. To stem the tide, Gaxim sends adventurers directly into the smoking operations at Windshear Crag. By targeting the frontline Venture Co. Loggers and Deforesters, travelers give Gaxim the respite he needs to organize his workshop and devise his next line of defense: strategic, controlled high explosives.

quest:1072.text: An Old Colleague. An Old Colleague is an Alliance quest given by the gnome engineer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. Looking to construct an extraordinarily potent device, Gaxim sends an adventurer all the way across the sea to Ironforge to track down an old acquaintance capable of synthesizing a hazardous explosive concoction. Completing this errand opens the door to procuring the volatile chemical compound known as Nitromirglyceronium. While stationed among the peaks of Stonetalon, Gaxim Rustfizzle conceives of his most ambitious engineering endeavor yet. Creating a mechanism of that scale requires specialized fuel far beyond typical gunpowder or crude oil. Specifically, Gaxim requires Nitromirglyceronium, also designated as NG-5, an explosive mix potent enough to guarantee destructive results should everything go according to plan. Formulating NG-5 is no simple task, and Gaxim knows of only one mind skilled enough to refine it: an old acquaintance named Lomac Gearstrip. Lomac resides far to the east in the gnome quarter of Tinker Town, tucked deep within the mountain stronghold of Ironforge. Entrusted with the long journey, the courier arrives only to be greeted by Lomac's immediate suspicion and paranoid questioning.

quest:1073.text: Ineptitude + Chemicals = Fun. Seeking an explosive countermeasure against the Venture Company in the Stonetalon Mountains, Alliance adventurers are sent across the sea to Ironforge. There, the eccentric gnome Lomac Gearstrip agrees to brew his volatile invention, Nitromirglyceronium, provided you fetch the necessary alchemical reagents. Gaxim Rustfizzle, stationed high in the craggy passes of the Stonetalon Mountains, needed potent explosives for the most advanced device he had yet devised against the Venture Company. For that, he turned to an eccentric former colleague living in Ironforge: Lomac Gearstrip. Lomac is the creator of Nitromirglyceronium, a substance so inherently unstable and destructive that he finds the prospect of anyone using it hilarious, regardless of who gets blown apart in the process. Despite Lomac's eagerness to see goblin machinery—and possibly the adventurer—blown into pieces, his workshop in Ironforge is entirely out of the finished compound. Before he will brew a fresh batch of Nitromirglyceronium, Lomac demands common alchemical draughts: Minor Mana Potions and Elixirs of Minor Fortitude. In his eyes, forcing an adventurer to gather these ingredients serves a dual purpose, ensuring he has the raw reagents needed for the reaction while proving they possess at least a shred of respect for the craft of alchemy.

quest:1074.text: Ineptitude + Chemicals = Fun. This errand delivers a canister of volatile NG-5 from the tinker Lomac Gearstrip to Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. Gaxim requires this unstable chemical to create a potent igniter for several wagons packed with dynamite. The resulting blast forms a critical distraction for Alliance operations in the disputed crags. Gnomish engineering often balances brilliance on the razor edge of catastrophe, and Nitromirglyceronium—or NG-5—is no exception. Lomac Gearstrip hands over the unstable compound with a stern warning: handle it with extreme care, or risk blowing yourself to pieces on the road back to Gaxim Rustfizzle.

quest:1075.text: A Scroll from Mauren. "A Scroll from Mauren" is an Alliance errand carrying word between gnome ingenuity and human arcane craft. The inventive Gaxim Rustfizzle requires a specialized spell to remotely trigger his volatile NG-5 explosives, dispatching couriers to consult with mage Collin Mauren in the heart of Stormwind. Gnomish engineering is legendary for ambitious concepts, but safe execution often requires clever solutions. When Gaxim Rustfizzle set out to design an explosive payload capable of remote activation, mechanical fuses proved insufficient. Rather than relying purely on mechanical timers or trailing cords, Gaxim envisioned a device that would detonate the NG-5 explosives at the push of a single button from a safe vantage point. To bridge the gap between volatile powder and instantaneous trigger, he turned his sights toward arcane magic. To acquire the necessary spellwork, Gaxim directs travelers across the kingdom to Stormwind's bustling Mage Quarter. There resides Collin Mauren, a human spellcaster whose practical understanding of the arcane makes him an ideal partner for ambitious tinkers. Mauren ponders the delicate problem of binding explosive ignition to a distant command, marking the first step in assembling the arcane incantation required to arm Gaxim's hazardous project.

quest:1076.text: Devils in Westfall. "Devils in Westfall" is an Alliance errand undertaken for Collin Mauren in the Mage Quarter of Stormwind. Tasked with aiding an eccentric experiment by the gnome inventor Gaxim Rustfizzle, adventurers are sent into the desolate plains of Westfall to gather volatile debris from living dust devils. The collected dust provides the raw magical component needed to enchant a specialized messaging scroll. The wizard Collin Mauren is assisting the tinkerer Gaxim Rustfizzle with an unusual venture, but arcane work requires specialized reagents. To enchant a scroll capable of carrying Gaxim's desired messaging spell, Mauren cannot rely on simple ink and vellum alone. The swirling elemental magic trapped within Westfall's native dust devils provides the exact volatile medium needed to bind the spell into parchment form. Westfall was once the fertile breadbasket of Stormwind, but drought, banditry, and neglect have left the land arid and wild. Swirling dust devils now roam the untamed fields, posing a hazard to travelers and lone homesteaders alike. By defeating one of these living whirlwinds and gathering its residue, adventurers retrieve the focused elemental essence required to bring the mage's enchantment to life.

quest:1077.text: Special Delivery for Gaxim. Special Delivery for Gaxim represents the return leg of an Alliance courier mission between Stormwind City and the wilds of Kalimdor. Collin Mauren provides a specialized Scroll of Messaging to take back to the gnome tinkerer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. The scroll contains the arcane component needed to construct a remote explosive against local deforestation efforts. Gaxim Rustfizzle's efforts to sabotage the destructive operations of the Venture Company require unconventional solutions. Having concocted an explosive compound called NG-5, the tinkerer found himself lacking a reliable means of remote detonation. Rather than turning to crude fuses, Gaxim enlisted help across the Great Sea, reaching out to Collin Mauren in the Mage Quarter of Stormwind to acquire an enchanted Scroll of Messaging.

quest:1085.text: On Guard in Stonetalon. On Guard in Stonetalon directs Alliance travelers from Kaela Shadowspear to Gaxim Rustfizzle at their camp near Windshear Crag. Facing rampant despoilment by the Venture Company, an otherwise unlikely pair—a cautious night elf sentinel and an eccentric gnome tinkerer—join forces to safeguard the mountain pass. Night elves and gnomes rarely share common ground, especially when it comes to technology and the natural world. In the crags of Stonetalon Mountains, however, necessity bridges the cultural gulf. With the rapacious Venture Company carving out the wilderness and felling ancient trees, the sentinel Kaela Shadowspear has recognized that pure martial prowess alone cannot overcome industrialized pillaging. Welcoming gnome ingenuity into sacred Kaldorei territory demonstrates just how precarious the situation has become. Gaxim Rustfizzle represents the eccentric pragmatism of the Alliance's smaller allies. While night elf society famously turned its back on arcane excess millennia ago, Gaxim believes that abstaining from magic and technical innovation leaves them vulnerable. By pairing alchemy and engineering with a touch of arcane discipline, Gaxim aims to convince his Kaldorei hosts that practical science can defend nature just as effectively as bow and glaive.

quest:1093.text: Super Reaper 6000. Super Reaper 6000 is a quest offered by the disgruntled goblin tinkerer Ziz Fizziks in the Windshear Crag of the Stonetalon Mountains. Looking to curry favor with his new boss Sputtervalve, Ziz hires adventurers to infiltrate the local Venture Company logging operation and steal the schematic blueprints for a colossal woodcutting machine designed by his rival, the gnome Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle. The Venture Trading Company has carved an industrial scar straight into the heart of the Stonetalon Mountains, ruthlessly deforesting Windshear Crag. Yet beneath the smog and spinning blades lies petty corporate rivalry. Ziz Fizziks, a goblin engineer recently cast out of the Venture Company's ranks, has found employment with Sputtervalve. Eager to cement his position and show off his value, Ziz seeks to procure the Venture Company's most prized mechanical asset: the blueprints for their massive automated lumber engine, the Super Reaper 6000.

quest:1094.text: Further Instructions. Further Instructions is a delivery task connecting the chaotic logging operations of the Stonetalon Mountains to the trade hub of Ratchet. The disgruntled tinkerer Ziz Fizziks sends a courier with stolen blueprints and internal documents to his counterpart, Sputtervalve, aiming to turn corporate espionage into personal advantage. When Ziz Fizziks was booted out of the Venture Company's logging operations in the Windshear Crag, he did not leave empty-handed. Bitter over his dismissal, Fizziks snatched up an assortment of sensitive documents, internal manuals, and technical schematics, culminating in the prized blueprints for the experimental Super Reaper 6000. Desperate to find a buyer or ally willing to exploit the data, he sealed the gathered secrets into an envelope marked for Ratchet. The recipient of the stolen documents is Sputtervalve, an engineer stationed within the neutral port of Ratchet in the Barrens. While Sputtervalve harbors little personal affection or trust for Fizziks, the rivalry with the Venture Company makes the offering impossible to refuse. The Steamwheedle-aligned goblins are constantly looking for ways to diminish their ruthless competitor's footprint while happily reverse-engineering any superior mechanical innovations they stumble across.

quest:1133.text: Journey to Astranaar. Journey to Astranaar is an introductory Alliance quest guiding newcomers arriving on the Kalimdor coast to the inland heart of Ashenvale. Directed by Fiora Longears at Theramore, travelers make their way north toward Ashenvale to report to Shindrell Swiftfire in Astranaar. It marks an adventurer's entry into the growing conflicts surrounding the night elves' ancestral forest. Alliance travelers arriving in Dustwallow Marsh aboard the ferry from Menethil Harbor often look for purpose in northern Kalimdor. At Theramore, Fiora Longears directs capable hands to move deeper inland toward Astranaar, the main night elven settlement within Ashenvale. The journey follows winding paths under ancient, shadowed canopies, leading straight into a forest strained by war and unrest. Curiously, Fiora tells travelers not to bother mentioning her name when arriving in Astranaar, stating plainly that Shindrell Swiftfire does not know her. Her role is simply to funnel fresh Alliance talent where it is needed most. Upon arriving, Shindrell readily welcomes any able-bodied defender, acknowledging that while Ashenvale remains breathtaking, it is no longer the peaceful sanctuary it once was.

quest:1134.text: Pridewings of Stonetalon. Shindrell reports an unconfirmed claim: Concerned about covert Horde attacks, the Sentinels in Astranaar seek to intercept a deadly weapon before it can strike their people. Intelligence from Theramore reveals that orc assassins harvest toxic venom from the wyverns of Stonetalon Mountains for clandestine raids. To protect their fragile border, Alliance scouts are dispatched south to harvest the venom sacs first and starve the enemy of their lethal poison. Though open war has not been declared between the Alliance and the Horde across northern Kalimdor, the peace between them is razor-thin. Skirmishes break out under thick forest canopies, and quiet, deniable strikes have replaced full-scale armies. Sentinel commanders in Astranaar maintain constant vigilance against covert enemy movements, knowing that complacency could cost them their sanctuary. Shindrell reports an unconfirmed claim: Intelligence passed from secretive contacts in Theramore brought word of a sinister enterprise underway in the crags of Stonetalon. Orcish stalkers have been gathering venom from wild pridewings around Mirkfallon Lake, using the potent biological agent to coat their blades for fatal ambush raids against Alliance personnel. To blunt the threat, Shindrell Swiftfire directs champions to cull the beasts and seize the venom sacs before Horde agents can harvest them. Ordering the destruction of native beasts weighs heavily on the night elves, who hold deep reverence for Kalimdor's wilderness. Shindrell herself laments that innocent creatures must suffer for a war they have no role in choosing. Yet in the grim calculus of border defense, denying an enemy lethal arms takes precedence over ecological preservation.

quest:124.text: A Baying of Gnolls. Verner Osgood, the stable master in Lakeshire, finds his business under siege by gnolls raiding south from the Redridge foothills. Already strained by Blackrock orc incursions, he asks travelers to clear out the brutes and mystics threatening his livestock. Running a stable in Lakeshire has become increasingly hazardous. Blackrock orcs command the heights of the region, while packs of gnolls roam the surrounding ridges. For Verner Osgood, the situation reached a breaking point when aggressive gnoll raiding bands crept close to the northern borders of his paddocks, preying on any horses that wandered too close to the bluffs.

quest:126.text: Howling in the Hills. Howling in the Hills is an Alliance bounty offered by Verner Osgood in Lakeshire to hunt down Yowler, the fearsome alpha leading the Redridge gnolls. With Stormwind's military stretched too thin fighting the Blackrock orcs to defend the local borders, Lakeshire relies on visiting adventurers to break the gnoll pack's command. Even after culling the lesser gnolls raiding the paths around Lakeshire, their ominous calls continue to echo through the Redridge ridges. Verner Osgood, Lakeshire's hardworking farrier, recognizes that killing scouts and scavengers will never stem the tide as long as their pack leader remains alive. Rising above the rabble is Yowler, an exceptionally cunning and massive gnoll whose calls direct the pack across the hills. Verner tasks adventurers with hunting down the beast and severing his paw to ensure the howling is silenced once and for all. This contract highlights the grim reality facing the eastern borders of the kingdom of Stormwind. With the missing King Varian Wrynn and regency disputes paralyzing high command, royal soldiers are focused almost exclusively on the entrenched Blackrock orc clans in the north. Everyday settlements like Lakeshire are left completely undefended against native menaces like gnolls, forcing townsfolk like Verner Osgood to organize their own bounties to prevent their homes from being overrun.

quest:127.text: Selling Fish. Dockmaster Baren manages the bustling pier at Lakeshire, but finding fresh stock for his trade has grown difficult. He pays travelers to haul in spotted sunfish, a prized local staple of Lake Everstill that has become dangerous to gather due to the encroaching murlocs. Lake Everstill is known throughout the surrounding lands for its spotted sunfish, a delicate catch that remains in perpetual demand among the townspeople and passing merchants. Yet despite the abundance beneath the lake's surface, the town's supplies regularly run thin. With Lakeshire stretched to its limits under various local threats, even basic commerce requires the help of freelance adventurers. Normally, local anglers would have little trouble satisfying Dockmaster Baren's orders. However, the rise of aggressive murloc tribes along the shallows and banks has driven ordinary townsfolk away from the water. Travelers looking to fulfill Baren's request must either cast their own lines while watching their backs, or claim the catch directly from the foraging murlocs that plague the shores.

quest:1472.text: Devourer of Souls. Devourer of Souls is an introductory step in a Forsaken warlock's journey to summon and bind a succubus. Directed by Carendin Halgar in the Undercity's Temple of the Damned, the practitioner must confer with his assistant, Godrick Farsan, to learn how to lure such a creature from the Twisting Nether. The ritual demands an irresistible stimulus: the hearts of pure and loving mortals. Carendin Halgar teaches that a succubus cannot simply be pulled across the threshold on command; it must be enticed. Driven by an insatiable hunger to ruin virtue and consume mortal essence, the demon requires a specific lure. The warlock's strategy relies on exploiting this singular desire by offering up the hearts of genuinely virtuous, loving men as bait. Halgar directs his acolytes to Godrick Farsan, who knows where such rare quarry can be harvested. Located deeper within the Temple of the Damned, Godrick Farsan assists Carendin with the practical preparations of demonic binding. Though Farsan has lost his physical eyesight, he claims his condition grants him a profound second sight—allowing him to perceive underlying spiritual currents and far-off souls with uncanny clarity. He serves as the guide for locating the pure hearts necessary to draw the demon forth.

quest:1474.text: The Binding. The Binding is the final initiation in an Undercity warlock's journey to summon and command a succubus. Directed by Carendin Halgar, the practitioner uses pure hearts to draw a demon from the Twisting Nether into a ritual circle, subjugating its will through combat. Within the dark alcoves of the Magic Quarter, Forsaken warlocks refine their command over demonic entities. Summoning a succubus is considered a critical rite of passage. Unlike the brute force of a voidwalker or the minor malice of an imp, a succubus wields seductive and mental enchantments capable of ensnaring the caster. Carendin Halgar requires initiates to prove their mind and magic are ironclad before trusting them with permanent dominion over such an entity.

quest:1476.text: Hearts of the Pure. Hearts of the Pure is a sinister warlock trial assigned in the Undercity by Godrick Farsan on behalf of Carendin Halgar. In order to prepare the ritual bait needed to bind a succubus, an aspiring summoner must hunt down and butcher two uniquely righteous human men. Their pure hearts serve as an irresistible temptation for the demonic temptress awaiting summoning. Binding a succubus requires an understanding of temptation that cuts both ways. While the Nether's sirens prey upon desire and ruin, nothing draws them out of the Twisting Nether quite like untainted virtue ripe for corruption. Within the Temple of the Damned, master summoner Carendin Halgar delegates the groundwork to Godrick Farsan, who scours human lands for souls whose goodness remains pristine and unbroken. Farsan identifies two distinct paragons of virtue. The first is Dalin Forgewright, an honorable man attending to desperate Lordaeron refugees barred from sanctuary outside the sealed Greymane Wall in southern Silverpine. The second is Comar Villard, a faithful husband tirelessly searching the perilous marshlands of the Wetlands for any trace of his lost wife. To a Forsaken warlock, their devotion, empathy, and loyalty make them prime sacrifices.

quest:1483.text: Ziz Fizziks. This quest sends travelers from Ratchet to check on Ziz Fizziks, a disgruntled goblin engineer stationed on the western ridge of Windshear Crag. Offended when the Venture Company hired a gnome engineer over him, Ziz defected to the Tinkers' Union under Sputtervalve's demanding direction. The Venture Company relies on ruthless exploitation and mechanical innovation, but it crossed a line for Ziz Fizziks when it brought on a gnome engineer named Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle. Deeply insulted by having to work alongside a gnomish rival, Ziz immediately sought a way out. He reached out to Sputtervalve, a contact representing the Tinkers' Union, begging for a transfer away from Gerenzo's oversight. Securing a new position with the Tinkers' Union did not grant Ziz the easy life he anticipated. Stationed on the western edge of Windshear Crag, he quickly discovered that Sputtervalve is just as much of a slave driver as any Venture Company foreman. Even so, Ziz considers heavy labor under a demanding goblin superior far preferable to sharing an engineering workshop with a gnome.

quest:150.text: Murloc Poachers. Dockmaster Baren of Lakeshire needs adventurers to thin the swelling ranks of murlocs along Lake Everstill before they deplete the town's primary food source. What begins as a practical pest-control bounty raises an unsettling ecological question: why are coastal creatures settling so deep into the inland mountains? Lake Everstill is the lifeblood of Lakeshire, keeping the mountain town fed and supplying its market with fresh catches. When large tribes of murlocs began dropping anchor along the shallows, Dockmaster Baren realized the town faced an ecological crisis. The ravenous fish-men were aggressively scouring the waters, threatening to wipe out the local fish populations entirely if left unchecked. Murlocs are typically coastal scavengers, making their massive presence high up in the Redridge Mountains an unusual sight. Dockmaster Baren openly wonders why they have traveled so far from the open ocean. Whether driven inland by maritime predators, fleeing territorial squabbles, or drawn by Lake Everstill's bountiful waters, their displacement hints at deeper disruptions elsewhere in the region.

quest:1507.text: Devourer of Souls. Devourer of Souls is the opening task in an aspiring Horde warlock's journey to summon and command a succubus. Offered by Gan'rul Bloodeye deep within the Cleft of Shadow, the quest sends the practitioner across the cavern to consult the ancient warlock Cazul on how to lure and bind such a manipulative demon. Warlocks of the Horde who have mastered lesser demons like the imp and the voidwalker eventually reach a point where brute force is no longer enough. Gan'rul Bloodeye, overseer of dark arts beneath Orgrimmar, judges when a warlock is ready to reach into the Twisting Nether for a succubus—a creature notorious for turning the minds of the frail against themselves. Binding such a fiend requires subtle methods rather than sheer strength. Because a succubus preys on mortal desires, it cannot be summoned by raw incantations alone; it must be baited into our world with an object imbued with pure love and devotion. Unwilling or unable to provide such a relic himself, Gan'rul directs the summoner to Cazul, an ancient warlock lurking within the Cleft of Shadow whose extensive knowledge of the arcane and demonic rites guides the next phase of the ritual.

quest:1508.text: Blind Cazul. Blind Cazul is a transitional step in the Horde warlock trial to bind a succubus. After being directed by the coven leaders in the Cleft of Shadow, an initiate seeks out the sightless warlock Cazul, who points toward an object of intense emotion needed for the ritual. Subjugating a demonic minion requires more than raw willpower; certain creatures of the Twisting Nether must be drawn across the veil by their innate cravings. A succubus, known as a devourer of souls, responds eagerly to mortal longing, sorrow, and unfulfilled desire. Cazul understands this well, recognizing immediately why an aspiring summoner has sought him out. Despite his physical blindness, Cazul remains sharply attuned to the quiet lives and tragedies unfolding within Orgrimmar's red ramparts. Rather than sending the warlock directly to battle, he directs them to an orc woman named Zankaja living atop the bluffs near the wind rider roost. Zankaja has been anxiously waiting for the return of her mate, Dogran, harboring the very despair that demons find irresistible.

quest:1509.text: News of Dogran. This quest sends Horde warlocks from the clefts of Orgrimmar into the dry expanses of the Barrens in search of a missing grunt named Dogran. His mate, Zankaja, fears the worst after days of silence, sending the practitioner to question Dogran's superior at the Crossroads. Unraveling Dogran's fate forms a crucial step in the warlock ritual to bind a succubus. On the bluffs of Orgrimmar, Zankaja waits in quiet dread. Her mate Dogran was assigned to the Crossroads on an honorable promotion, yet his scheduled return has long passed without a single word. Unaware of the intricate dark arts pulling strings behind the scenes, she reaches out to a sympathetic traveler to seek answers from his commander, Gazrog.

quest:1510.text: News of Dogran. This quest sends Horde adventurers deep into the foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains to contact the Darkspear troll Ken'zigla at Malaka'jin. An injured grunt from Camp Taurajo named Dogran lies wounded, and the first runner sent to fetch a lifesaving herbal draught never returned. Dogran, a Horde grunt stationed at Camp Taurajo in the southern Barrens, was grievously wounded during a skirmish against entrenched quilboar. The grunts with him made it back and tried to rescue him, but his wounds had festered so badly that they were afraid to move him without patching him up first. Desperate for a potent remedy, Taurajo sent word north to the Crossroads, hoping to procure a traditional healing draught prepared by the jungle trolls of Malaka'jin.

quest:1511.text: Ken'zigla's Draught. Ken'zigla's Draught is an urgent courier task in the Horde warlock chain to summon a succubus. Entrusted with a potent medicinal concoction from Malaka'jin in the Stonetalon Mountains, the warlock must rush across Kalimdor to Camp Taurajo to save an operative named Dogran. In the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, the troll apothecary Ken'zigla anticipated trouble. Knowing that an earlier emissary sent to secure medicine for the missing scout Dogran never made it back, Ken'zigla prepared a second dose of his potent restorative draught. The concoction is volatile and powerful: half a dose grants a mortally wounded soldier the vigor to move without causing his injuries to hemorrhage, while the rest must be withheld until the next day to complete recovery.

quest:1512.text: Love's Gift. Love's Gift is the penultimate quest in the Horde warlock chain to summon and bind a succubus. After being tracked down and revived in the Barrens, the dying Grunt Dogran relinquishes a treasured keepsake to provide the bait necessary for the dark ritual. To summon and subjugate a succubus, a warlock requires a talisman of intense, unblemished emotion. Succubi feed on mortal desire and pervert genuine affection into anguish. Dogran's pendant carries the weight of authentic devotion and tragic parting. Returned to Gan'rul Bloodeye in the shadowy clefts of Orgrimmar, the talisman is cleaned and polished so its radiant emotional resonance can lure the devourer of souls across the Twisting Nether.

quest:1513.text: The Binding. The Binding is the final trial in an aspiring Horde warlock's quest to enslave a succubus in Orgrimmar. By using the devotion bound up in Dogran's Pendant at Neeru Fireblade's summoning circle, the warlock wrenches a demon from the Twisting Nether and breaks its will through force of arms and spellcraft. Beneath the clefts of Orgrimmar, deep within the tent of Neeru Fireblade, lies a summoning circle prepared for such hazardous work. Under the tutelage of Gan'rul Bloodeye, the warlock activates the rune-scribed circle and battles the summoned seductress. A warlock cannot simply call a demon into service; they must overpower it in single combat, bending its malevolent spirit to their sovereign will.

quest:1515.text: Dogran's Captivity. Dogran's Captivity is a vital trial in an aspiring Horde warlock's training, sending practitioners into the heart of a quilboar camp to rescue a captured orc warrior. Entrusted with a revitalizing concoction, the warlock must locate the battered Grunt Dogran and supply him with the strength needed to escape his captors. Grunt Logmar at Camp Taurajo refuses to risk Horde military manpower on a costly raid against the entrenched quilboar, leaving the fate of his comrade Dogran entirely in the hands of an enterprising warlock. Armed solely with Ken'zigla's Draught, the rescuer must venture north among the brambles and hostile camps to locate where Dogran is held captive.

quest:1529.text: Call of Water. Call of Water is an initiation rite that directs rising Horde shaman from the heights of Thunder Bluff toward the eastern shores of the Barrens. To commune with the cleansing element of water, an initiate must seek out the recluse Islen Waterseer. This meeting marks the first step on a spiritual journey to earn the Water Totem. Having mastered the unyielding earth and the untamed flame, an aspiring shaman is eventually deemed ready to study the deeper mysteries of the elements. In Thunder Bluff, trainers like Xanis Flameweaver recognize when a student has shown enough discipline to approach the fluid, cleansing spirit of water. The journey requires leaving the windswept mesas of Mulgore behind and traveling east across the sun-scorched plains of the Barrens. The path leads to Islen Waterseer, a quiet mystic who lives away from the bustling settlements, residing in a humble fishing shack on the eastern coast south of Ratchet and the mouth of the Southfury River. Standing at the edge of the great ocean, Islen reads the readiness of travelers by how the elements linger about them. Seeing the steady earth, the brisk wind, and the warmth of fire already bound to the seeker's spirit, she prepares them for the trials required to understand water's purity.

quest:163.text: Raven Hill. Reports of shifting shadows and flickering window light in the abandoned settlement of Raven Hill have set the Night Watch on edge. Dispatched by Elaine Carevin in Darkshire, travelers are sent west across the haunted woods to confront whatever sinister presence has taken shelter among the ruins. To the rangers of the Night Watch, the far western edge of Duskwood has long been surrendered to the dead and the wilderness. Yet complete abandonment would be preferable to unexpected activity. Calor, a watcher patrolling the gloomy roads, noticed movement among the silent houses of Raven Hill two nights in a row, punctuated by the unsettling flicker of a lantern in a window. In a land plagued by ghouls, skeletons, and beasts, any unexplained signs of life demand immediate investigation.

quest:1653.text: The Test of Righteousness. The Test of Righteousness marks the transition from defending the innocent in Westfall to embarking on the construction of a paladin's sacred weapon. Entrusted by Duthorian Rall, the initiate travels to Ironforge to bring glad tidings to the devout smith Jordan Stilwell. Having stood guard over Daphne Stilwell during a harrowing Defias ambush on her Westfall homestead, a paladin initiate returns to Cathedral Square to report. Duthorian Rall recognizes that word must reach her husband, Jordan Stilwell, who left for Ironforge believing his family in jeopardy. Rall sends the young knight to deliver the relief in person, serving both as an act of fellowship and the prelude to a deeper undertaking. Jordan Stilwell was originally destined for the holy order of paladins, yet chose to honor his father's craft as a master weapon-smith without ever forsaking his faith. Setting up his anvil outside the gates of Ironforge to work in the bracing mountain air, Jordan relies on his spiritual devotion to guide his hammer. Upon hearing that his wife survived the Defias assault, his profound gratitude moves him to aid the paladin in forging a blessed weapon of righteousness.

quest:167.text: Oh Brother. . .. "Oh Brother. . ." is an Alliance mission given by Wilder Thistlenettle in Stormwind City. Distraught over a cave-in during an expedition into the depths beneath Moonbrook, Wilder asks adventurers to search the labyrinthine mines for his missing sibling, Foreman Thistlenettle, or recover his Explorers' League Badge. Wilder Thistlenettle and his brother entered the cavernous subterranean tunnels beneath Moonbrook as members of a mining company. However, things turned catastrophic when hostile thieves swarmed the area and a violent cave-in sealed off the lower tunnels. Wilder managed to escape to Stormwind, but his brother and the rest of the crew were left trapped behind the rubble.

quest:1698.text: Yorus Barleybrew. Yorus Barleybrew is an Alliance warrior summons directing seasoned fighters out of Stormwind toward the borderlands of Redridge. Issued by martial trainers across the Alliance capitals, it sends ambitious combatants to meet an eccentric dwarf laying down a deadly challenge at the Lakeshire Inn. Warrior trainers across the Alliance capitals, including Kelv Sternhammer, Wu Shen, and Darnath Bladesinger, keep a close eye on fighters who have outgrown basic drills. When an apprentice proves their mettle around their twentieth season, these masters pass along word of a dwarf named Yorus Barleybrew. Rather than issuing a standard military directive, Barleybrew has put out an open wager and a test of arms to any Alliance warrior bold enough to answer. Barleybrew has stationed himself at the tavern in Lakeshire, right on the front lines of Redridge's struggle against encroaching gnolls and Blackrock orcs. Those who track him down find a boastful dwarf with a hearty drink in hand, ready to size up any challenger who claims to possess real fighting spirit. For warriors seeking to prove themselves beyond the safe cobbled streets of the capital, his trial marks an initiation into harsher frontier battles.

quest:1716.text: Devourer of Souls. Devourer of Souls is a pivotal rite of passage for Alliance warlocks dispatched from Stormwind to learn the summoning of a succubus. Directed by Gakin the Darkbinder, initiates must trek halfway across the world into the hazardous wildlands of the Barrens to seek counsel from Takar the Seer. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder instructs promising warlocks on their next major summons: the succubus. Described as a devourer of souls, a destroyer of hearts, and a dominator of minds, this demonic entity cannot be summoned blindly into Azeroth. It requires a potent lure, specifically an object tied to pure love, to tease it forth from the Twisting Nether so that the practitioner may defeat and bind it. Procuring such a token demands wisdom that Stormwind's covens cannot provide locally. To track down the required catalyst, Gakin sends his pupils across the Great Sea to Kalimdor. Deep in the arid expanse of the Barrens, near the Horde settlement of Camp Taurajo, sits Takar the Seer. For an Alliance warlock, reaching Takar requires braving wilderness heavily patrolled by hostile centaur, quilboar, and Horde warriors, serving as an unstated test of survival before the summoner can even begin preparing the ritual.

quest:1717.text: Gakin's Summons. A summons delivered to promising Alliance warlocks in Ironforge, directing them south to Stormwind. Gakin the Darkbinder awaits beneath the city's Mage Quarter to oversee their advancement into commanding greater fiends. Demonology remains a practice conducted entirely in shadows across Alliance lands. In Ironforge, Lago Blackwrench quietly keeps tabs on wandering practitioners on behalf of the brotherhood in Stormwind. When a warlock shows sufficient mastery over their initial minions, word travels quickly. Lago passes along the directive: drop whatever business keeps you in the snowy mountains of Khaz Modan and report south without delay. Deep beneath the cobblestones of Stormwind's Mage Quarter, beneath the tavern known as The Slaughtered Lamb, Gakin the Darkbinder coordinates the development of the city's warlocks. Gakin views every capable student as a valuable, hazardous investment. Receiving his summons marks the threshold of true demonic binding, beginning the trials required to subjugate a succubus from the Twisting Nether.

quest:1738.text: Heartswood. Heartswood is an Alliance warlock quest that sends practitioners deep into Ashenvale to recover the branch of an ancient, tragic tree. Sent by the hermit Takar the Seer on behalf of Gakin the Darkbinder, warlocks seek this romantic relic as a potent bait to lure and subjugate a succubus in Stormwind. According to Takar the Seer, the Heartswood tree sprang from the spot where two night elf lovers, Anathera and Latherion, fell together during the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago. Nourished by their final breaths and eternal devotion, the tree grew as a pure emblem of undying romance. To mortal senses it is a sacred tragic monument, but to practitioners of the dark arts, concentrated emotional energy makes potent magical fuel. Succubi feed upon mortal passions, desire, and emotional torment. Takar realizes that ordinary temptations pale in comparison to an artifact suffused with thousands of years of pure, undying devotion. A piece of the Heartswood provides Gakin the Darkbinder with the exact catalyst required to bait one of these cunning demons across the Nether into the summoning circle in Stormwind's Mage Quarter.

quest:1739.text: The Binding. The Binding is the final initiation ritual for Alliance warlocks seeking to command a succubus in Stormwind. Using the enchanted core obtained from the Heartswood, the practitioner enters the summoning circle beneath The Slaughtered Lamb to drag forth and physically overpower the demon. Once defeated, the demon's will is chained, binding its servitude to the summoner. Hidden beneath the floorboards of The Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter lies a cavernous crypt dedicated to forbidden arts. Far from the watchful eyes of the city watch and the Cathedral of Light, the city's covert warlock enclave conducts its most dangerous rituals here. Summoning circles etched into stone channel the raw forces of the Nether, allowing ambitious initiates to pierce the veil between worlds. Summoning a succubus requires far more than merely chanting incantations. A warlock must bring a focus—in this case, the prepared Heartswood Core—and cast a ritual of breach at the circle. Succubi are known to corrupt, seduce, and overwhelm even fortified minds. To establish absolute mastery, the summoner must cut the beast down in single combat, banishing its physical form back to the Twisting Nether while securing its true tether.

quest:1793.text: The Tome of Valor. The Tome of Valor is a foundational trial for Alliance paladins coming into their own. Directed by paladin mentors in Stormwind and Ironforge, initiates are challenged to prove that their courage and devotion to protecting the innocent match their martial prowess. To wield the Holy Light in battle requires more than heavy armor and martial discipline. As young paladins reach greater heights in their training, instructors in the Cathedral of Light and the Hall of Mysteries demand proof of their inner resolve. The lessons of the Tome of Valor test an initiate's readiness to confront terrifying evils—from dragons to demons—without faltering or abandoning those who cannot defend themselves. Bravery under mortal threat is considered as essential to a holy warrior as their weapon and shield. Through the trials laid out in the Tome of Valor, paladins learn that raw strength is hollow without an unwavering vow to shelter the helpless. Facing genuine peril ensures that when darkness falls upon the Alliance, its defenders will stand firm rather than break.

quest:1824.text: Trial at the Field of Giants. Trial at the Field of Giants is a warrior rites quest issued by Ruga Ragetotem at Camp Taurajo. As part of their training, martial aspirants are dispatched south into the swarming mounds of the Field of Giants to slay alien insectoid invaders. Candidates must harvest several still-twitching antennae and rush them back before the biological proof goes dormant. Warrior trainers among the Horde rarely accept mere martial competence without testing fortitude and urgency. Ruga Ragetotem challenges growing warriors at Camp Taurajo to prove themselves against an unfamiliar adversary. Aspirants are not just ordered to slay the encroaching creatures; they must sever fresh antennae and return to Taurajo within half an hour before the harvested tissue ceases twitching, demanding rapid navigation of the southern Barrens. The targets of the trial are the silithid hives burgeoning in the Field of Giants, nestled beneath massive fossilized ribcages. These crawling, chitinous insects are recent arrivals to the Barrens, disturbing the tauren hunters and shamans who watch the savannas. Ruga notes with dread that their presence bodes ill for Kalimdor, making the extermination test serve a dual purpose: proving a young warrior's combat instincts while gathering intelligence on a looming ecological menace.

quest:1825.text: Speak with Thun'grim. This errand directs rising Horde warriors to Thun'grim Firegaze, an acclaimed orc blacksmith camping in the Barrens. Having proved themselves through demanding physical trials, warriors are invited to have custom armor forged in recognition of their valor. The quest serves as the crucial bridge connecting general warrior testing with the crafting of Brutal Armor. After proving their mettle against the silithid hives during the Trial at the Field of Giants, Horde warriors earn more than simple praise from Ruga Ragetotem. Word of their endurance and martial prowess quickly reaches Thun'grim Firegaze, a renowned orc smith who maintains a camp perched on a ridge east of the Crossroads. Recognizing a warrior worthy of his craft, Thun'grim sends word that he wishes to fashion them an exceptional suit of battle mail. Thun'grim Firegaze does not forge for ordinary soldiers. For an armorsmith of his reputation, steel must match the spirit of the one who carries it into battle. Reaching his camp signifies that a warrior has advanced past simple militia drills and is ready to undertake the grueling, specialized tasks required to gather rare crafting reagents across Kalimdor.

quest:1999.text: Tools of the Trade. Tools of the Trade is an initiation mission for Horde rogues given by Mennet Carkad in the Undercity. Ordered by Lord Varimathras, agents must obtain lockpicking gear and infiltrate Ambermill to recover sensitive Kirin Tor reports detailing Dalaran's current state. Following the interrogation of one of their prisoners, the Deathstalkers learned that vital intelligence concerning the ruins of Dalaran lies hidden in Ambermill. Silverpine Forest remains a precarious front line, and the human mages guarding the village guard their communications fiercely. Under the orders of Lord Varimathras, Deathstalker handler Mennet Carkad directs promising operatives to bypass Kirin Tor sentries and secure the Dalaran Status Report. Unlike straightforward assassinations, this mission serves as a practical proving ground in infiltration and lockpicking. Operatives are outfitted with specialized thieves' tools from Estelle Gendry before marching into hostile Kirin Tor territory. Cracking the secured chest in Ambermill demonstrates that an operative has progressed beyond raw street brutality into an indispensable espionage asset for the Forsaken.

quest:20.text: Blackrock Menace. Marshal Marris of Lakeshire tasks adventurers with culling the aggressive Blackrock orcs encroaching upon Redridge. By seizing their battleworn axes, the town's defenders hope to break the siege tightening around the settlement. Lakeshire finds itself hemmed in on multiple fronts, but none pose so dire a threat as the Blackrock orcs spilling over from the fiery Burning Steppes. Having pushed south into Redridge, these veteran raiders have seized strongholds and roam the craggy passes. Their presence keeps the townspeople effectively penned inside the settlement, cutting off trade, foraging, and travel along the northern roads. Marshal Marris, commander of the beleaguered Lakeshire guard, cannot spare a detachment to assault their positions outright. Instead, he enlists roaming adventurers to bleed the invaders' forward scouts and foot soldiers. By demanding their crude, battleworn axes as proof of death, Marris seeks to thin the invaders' numbers both around Stonewatch to the north and in the rugged pockets of southeastern Redridge.

quest:2040.text: Underground Assault. Underground Assault is an Alliance quest offered by Shoni the Shilent in Stormwind City's Dwarven District. Tasked with aiding the displaced gnomes, adventurers venture into the Deadmines to salvage an intact power core from a goblin shredder. This stolen component is destined to power drilling machines intended to spearhead the liberation of Gnomeregan. Following the catastrophic fall of Gnomeregan to the primitive troggs, surviving gnomish tinkerers have been forced into exile across Khaz Modan and Stormwind. Rather than wallowing in defeat, engineers like Shoni the Shilent are already devising mechanical operations to breach their lost home. The primary obstacle is the dense, subterranean rock surrounding the technocratic city, requiring massive tunneling engines known as gyrodrillmatic excavationators. Lacking the necessary localized power grids in human lands, the gnomes have turned their sights to an unlikely and volatile alternative: goblin heavy machinery operating in the criminal underworld. Deep within the twisting shafts of the Deadmines in Westfall, Edwin VanCleef's Defias Brotherhood employs goblin engineers to manufacture war machines, including a fully operational goblin shredder. Shoni directs Alliance operatives to infiltrate this foundry, destroy or dismantle the lumbering automaton, and recover its specialized heart—the Gnoam Sprecklesprocket. By commandeering the potent goblin power supply, the exiled gnomes gain the raw mechanical output needed to bore through the subterranean perimeter and launch a counteroffensive to reclaim Gnomeregan.

quest:2078.text: Gyromast's Revenge. Gelkak Gyromast seeks payback against the local murlocs who plundered his wrecked ship along the Darkshore coastline. To carry out his vendetta, the eccentric captain sends adventurers to reactivate his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100. Stranded upon the misty strands of Darkshore, Gelkak Gyromast refuses to accept defeat at the hands of the shore-dwelling murlocs. Having salvaged the pieces needed to fuel his schemes, the eccentric captain sets his sights on complete retaliation against the tribe and their chief. Rather than wading into the surf with cutlass in hand, Gelkak relies on heavy engineering to exact his vengeance, entrusting a winding key to any landlubber brave enough to handle his mechanical subordinate.

quest:2098.text: Gyromast's Retrieval. Shipwrecked on the misty coast of Darkshore, the eccentric gnome pirate Gelkak Gyromast seeks aid to restore his mechanical first mate. His vital winding key was shattered upon the rocks and scavenged by the local wildlife and murlocs. Recovering the three pieces is the first step toward getting his crew back in working order. Gelkak Gyromast is an odd sight along the gloomy sands of Darkshore: a gnome pirate stranded far from the typical sea routes of the South Seas. According to Gelkak, his vessel met an unfortunate end just off the coastline after being attacked and sunk by aggressive threshadons. Washing ashore amid the flotsam, he found himself utterly marooned and separated from his trusty crew. Gelkak's most pressing concern is not provisions or gold, but his first mate. Activating and operating this companion requires a specialized key, which shattered into three distinct fragments when Gelkak crashed onto the rocky shoals. Before he could gather the fragments, the indigenous wildlife—scuttling reef crawlers on the beach, towering foreststriders near the woods, and scavengers from the local Greymist murloc tribe—snatched the shiny metal pieces away.

quest:2282.text: Alther's Mill. Alther's Mill is a pivotal training assignment given to Alliance rogues by Lucius in Lakeshire. Dispatched to the nearby mill with a set of thieves' tools, initiates are tasked with infiltrating an area under Blackrock orc scrutiny to crack a locked chest and retrieve a token of thievery. In Lakeshire, rogue instructors do not bother with abstract lectures when a locked chest can teach the lesson faster. Lucius sends promising operatives northeast along the road to Alther's Mill, equipping them with their first set of thieves' tools. To earn their formal Certificate of Thievery, novices must slip into the abandoned mill, pick open Lucius's personal lockbox, and bring back the token cached within. While Alther's Mill was once an ordinary lumber outpost, it has recently drawn the dangerous attention of the Blackrock orcs encroaching upon Redridge. Lucius gleefully treats the encroaching warmongers as an added layer of practical examination. Prowling through enemy-held territory to pick locks undetected is precisely the kind of trial SI:7 expects its agents to survive.

quest:235.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. Issued by Warcaller Gorlach in Orgrimmar, this directive summons budding Horde adventurers northward beyond the Barrens into the ancient forests of Ashenvale. Players are directed to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post to participate in the ongoing hunt and reinforce the Horde's expanding frontier. Orgrimmar buzzes with martial fervor, but the young city requires vast amounts of timber, meat, and secure trade routes to sustain its growth. Warcaller Gorlach serves as the voice of the Horde's high command, directing seasoned wanderers and new blood alike toward active campaigns. For warriors coming of age in Durotar and the Barrens, the ancient woodlands of Ashenvale represent the next testing ground for both glory and survival. Crossing the northern border of the Barrens brings travelers directly into Ashenvale, where the Horde maintains two primary bastions: Splintertree Post nestled in the eastern woods and Zoram'gar Outpost along the western coast. Senani Thunderheart coordinates operations at Splintertree Post, organizing trackers and hunters to tame the beast-choked canopy and push back against hostile night elven sentinels disputing the Horde's claims.

quest:240.text: Return to Jitters. Return to Jitters concludes Chef Grual's culinary errand in Duskwood. Having prepared his infamous 'crab' cakes using the gooey legs of the local venom web spiders, Grual sends you back to the starving, terrified hermit at Raven Hill. Delivering the meal finally satisfies Jitters' desperate hunger. Duskwood is short on conventional livestock and sea life, leaving Chef Grual at the Scarlet Raven Tavern to improvise with whatever the blighted forest provides. His renowned 'Dusky Crab Cakes' contain no actual crab meat at all, relying instead on gooey legs harvested from the venom web spiders creeping through the wood. Grual considers this resourceful cooking; anyone with a delicate stomach might view it with horror. Jitters spends his days huddled at Raven Hill, utterly consumed by fright and paralyzed by whatever horrors drove him out of the woods. Weak with terror and unable to muster the courage to hunt or forage for himself, his empty stomach only amplifies his distress. Receiving the warm cakes brings a rare moment of relief to the trembling vagrant, who is far too hungry to question what kind of 'crab' Chef Grual used.

quest:2458.text: Deep Cover. Deep Cover is an undercover assignment given to promising Horde rogues by Shenthul in Orgrimmar. The mission dispatches the operative to the Venture Company drilling grounds at Sludge Fen to establish secret contact with an embedded agent of the Shattered Hand. The Shattered Hand operates as the clandestine intelligence and assassin guild of the Horde, quietly guarding Orgrimmar's interests through ruthlessly practical means. For an entire year, the guild labored to slip an operative into the hierarchy of the rapacious Venture Company. That asset, Taskmaster Fizzule, managed to ingratiate himself into their industrial drilling outpost north of Sludge Fen. Operating deep within mercenary lines leaves no margin for error. Because Fizzule maintains a ruthless persona to satisfy his corporate overseers, any unannounced visitor risks immediate attack. To verify their identity, arriving rogues must fire twin flares from a designated signaling gun within sight of his tower, approach quietly, and perform the secret salute of the Shattered Hand before receiving his report on the Venture Company's escalating schemes.

quest:2460.text: The Shattered Salute. The Shattered Salute is an initiation ritual overseen by Shenthul within the Cleft of Shadow in Orgrimmar. By learning this distinct sign of recognition, budding rogues are taught how to safely identify fellow operatives of the Shattered Hand in the field. Within the dark tunnels of the Cleft of Shadow, the Shattered Hand operates as the clandestine intelligence and assassination arm of Thrall's Horde. Given the dangerous and secretive nature of their assignments, operatives cannot rely on overt banners or standard military heraldry. Shenthul instructs newly inducted rogues in the Shattered Salute, a specific gesture meant to serve as an unmistakable, silent signal among allies. Mastering the salute is not merely a ceremonial exercise; it is vital tradecraft. Rogue agents sent into perilous territory or tasked with infiltrating rival factions must verify contacts without alerting bystanders or targets. Shenthul insists that an operative be able to recognize and mirror the gesture effortlessly before entrusting them with covert fieldwork.

quest:2478.text: Mission: Possible But Not Probable. This critical assignment tests a Horde rogue's stealth, thievery, and combat skills against a rogue Venture Company outpost in the northern Barrens. Operatives infiltrate an oil tower, assassinate Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix, and seize a potent chemical concoction for the Shattered Hand. North of the Sludge Fen oil rigs, the Venture Company maintains an isolated drilling tower. Under orders from Taskmaster Fizzule, an embedded Shattered Hand operative posing as a Venture Company supervisor, rogues are instructed to use classic underworld methods rather than outright assault. Fizzule asks rogues to pickpocket a key directly off Foreman Silixiz and keep it for him before mounting an ascent through heavily altered workers and sentries.

quest:2479.text: Hinott's Assistance. Hinott's Assistance is an urgent journey undertaken by Horde rogues suffering from a debilitating tropical toxin. Contracted during an infiltration mission in the Barrens, the affliction requires the specialized expertise of Serge Hinott in Tarren Mill. Seeking his aid promises both a life-saving cure and instruction in the art of concocting deadly poisons. Following the daring infiltration of the Venture Company's tower north of the Sludge Fen, rogues find themselves afflicted by Zanzil's altered mixture. The poison wreaks havoc on the body, dulling reflexes and threatening life itself. Recognizing the severity of the affliction, rogue trainer Shenthul in Orgrimmar admits that local remedies are inadequate and directs the poisoned operative across the sea to the Eastern Kingdoms. The search for a cure leads south through the continent of Lordaeron to the village of Tarren Mill in Hillsbrad Foothills. There resides Serge Hinott, an apothecary whose fascination with virulent brews makes him ideally suited to analyze the exotic sample. While ordinary healers recoiled from Zanzil's venom, Hinott treats the deadly compound with professional glee, eager to dissect the foul concoction and instruct worthy rogues in brewing their own venoms.

quest:276.text: Tramping Paws. Tramping Paws is an Alliance task given by Rethiel the Greenwarden at the Greenwarden's Grove in the Wetlands. Troubled by the surging Mosshide gnoll population near the Gate of Algaz, the bog beast protector tasks adventurers with culling their numbers before their fires and trampling paws ruin the bog. For many years, the Mosshide gnolls inhabited the Wetlands without utterly overwhelming its natural order. Lately, however, their pack numbers have exploded south toward the pass of Dun Algaz. Their heavy boots and pawprints trample rare fen flora, and their crude logging strips vital groves to feed their campsite blazes. Left unchecked, the burgeoning packs threaten to degrade the fragile marsh ecology. Rethiel the Greenwarden watches over the marsh with an eye for balance rather than civilization. To the Greenwarden, the issue is not that gnolls exist, but that their runaway population outstrips what the Wetlands can support. By driving Mosshide gnolls and mongrels back into manageable numbers, adventurers help preserve the wetlands and earn the reluctant approval of an ancient wilderness guardian.

quest:4021.text: Counterattack!. Following the systematic elimination of their local chieftains in the Barrens, the Kolkar centaur mount a desperate retaliation out of Desolace. An invading force marches directly upon Regthar Deathgate's outpost west of the Crossroads, culminating in a fierce confrontation with Warlord Krom'zar. The campaign against the Kolkar centaur in the Barrens struck deep into their tribal leadership. With Barak Kodobane, Verog the Dervish, and Hezrul Bloodmark dead, the remaining centaur found themselves shattered and without direction. In response to this humiliation, word traveled west across the mountains to their ancestral homeland in Desolace. Rather than scattering into the scrubland, a fresh contingent of hardened Kolkar warriors rallied and crossed into the Barrens, burning for blood and retribution against the fledgling Horde encampments.

quest:442.text: Assault on Fenris Isle. Assault on Fenris Isle is the climactic military directive issued by High Executor Hadrec to eradicate the Scourge stronghold in Silverpine Forest. To break the Lich King's grip upon Lake Lordamere, Forsaken agents are sent to storm Fenris Keep and take the head of the necromancer Thule Ravenclaw. For weeks, Fenris Isle has stood as a poisonous blister in the heart of Lake Lordamere. While the Forsaken secured the western roads and established their presence at the Sepulcher, the Scourge entrenched themselves inside Fenris Keep. Commanded by the powerful necromancer Thule Ravenclaw, this island outpost threatened not only Silverpine Forest but the southern waterways leading toward the Undercity itself. High Executor Hadrec recognizes that the Forsaken will never truly hold Silverpine while a servant of the Lich King conducts vile experiments right off their eastern shores.

quest:455.text: The Algaz Gauntlet. The Algaz Gauntlet is an urgent military mission to fight through Dun Algaz, a critical mountain pass linking Loch Modan to the Wetlands. Orcs of the Dragonmaw clan have entrenched themselves in the tunnels, threatening to sever Ironforge's vital lifeline to Menethil Harbor. Adventurers are tasked with cutting down the orcish vanguard and delivering word of the invasion to Valstag Ironjaw. Dun Algaz serves as the solitary overland mountain pass carving through the crags between Loch Modan and the marshy basin of the Wetlands. For the dwarves of Ironforge, this stone corridor is essential for trade, troop movements, and supplies heading to Menethil Harbor, the Alliance's primary coastal port in the region. Should the pass fall, Ironforge's connection to the western seas is effectively strangled, leaving isolated outposts cut off from dwarven reinforcements. While remnants of the Dragonmaw clan have long haunted the hills and ruins of the Wetlands following the Second War, their sudden, organized push into Dun Algaz marks an aggressive escalation. Instead of lingering in their marshland enclaves, Dragonmaw scouts and grunts have seized the tunnels and fortified the pass. Mountaineer Rockgar enlists brave Alliance travelers to shatter this blockade by slaying the encroaching orcs and carrying word of the assault directly to Valstag Ironjaw in Menethil Harbor.

quest:463.text: The Greenwarden. "The Greenwarden" is an Alliance breadcrumb quest directing travelers deeper into the marshes of the Wetlands. Sent by First Mate Fitzsimmons from Menethil Harbor, adventurers venture northeast into the swamp to seek out a mysterious entity rumored to dwell among the beasts. Around the docks of Menethil Harbor, sailors and wanderers trade breathless stories of a beast lurking out in the swamp. First Mate Fitzsimmons paints the Greenwarden as an appetite with legs, warning gullible seekers that stepping off the dry road means being bitten in two by 'ol' Greenie.' To the dockside folk, anything massive lurking out in the murky waters is just another man-eating hazard of the marsh.

quest:468.text: Report to Mountaineer Rockgar. Report to Mountaineer Rockgar is an Alliance breadcrumb quest directing adventurers north from the guard posts of Loch Modan toward Dun Algaz. Mountaineer Kadrell dispatches capable travelers to join Rockgar, who is organizing a vital expedition into the sodden lowlands of the Wetlands. It serves as the gateway passage connecting the dwarven homeland to northern territories. Dun Algaz represents the crucial artery between Loch Modan and the marshy expanses of the Wetlands. Built into the northern mountain ridge, the fortified pass has long guaranteed safe passage for trade, messengers, and military detachments moving between Ironforge and Alliance settlements further north. With tensions rising along the borders, Mountaineer Kadrell keeps a close watch on travellers passing through, recruiting hardy volunteers to reinforce the northern outposts.

quest:469.text: Daily Delivery. Daily Delivery is an errand on behalf of the dwarven hunter Einar Stonegrip, who asks travelers heading toward Menethil Harbor to deliver cured crocolisk hides to the local tanner. Rather than facing domestic friction at home, Einar relies on passing adventurers to keep his supply line moving. Out in the marshlands, Einar Stonegrip makes his living hunting the local wildlife, particularly the aggressive crocolisks that lurk along the waterways. While he gathers plenty of valuable skins, delivering them requires a trip home to Menethil Harbor. Reluctant to confront his wife Sida during a rough patch in their marriage, Einar prefers to stay in the field and hand his parcels off to passing travelers instead. The destination for these hides is James Halloran, a tanner operating within Menethil Harbor. Halloran relies on regular deliveries from local hunters to craft boots and cure leather for merchants and sailors passing through the port. Having noticed Einar's week-long absence, the tanner easily deduces the marital spat behind the proxy delivery, musing that his own wife might need to intervene and smooth things over with Sida.

quest:493.text: Journey to Hillsbrad Foothills. Journey to Hillsbrad Foothills is a Horde courier task connecting the Forsaken research efforts in Silverpine Forest with their outpost in Tarren Mill. Entrusted with sensitive notes from Apothecary Renferrel, the traveler journeys south into the disputed Hillsbrad Foothills to deliver vital biological research to Apothecary Lydon. This dispatch reflects the intense pressure Lady Sylvanas Windrunner places upon the Royal Apothecary Society to produce a weapon of mass devastation. Since breaking free from the Lich King's iron grip, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner has harbored a single-minded ambition: the development of a New Plague engineered to eradicate both living enemies and the Scourge. To achieve this, the Royal Apothecary Society operates under relentless pressure from the Banshee Queen. Because distance isolates their laboratories, researchers scattered across Lordaeron must continuously share raw chemical data and test findings to accelerate their sinister breakthrough. Apothecary Renferrel, operating out of the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, directs couriers to deliver his recent findings to his colleague, Apothecary Lydon. The trek winds south through the shadowed pine woods and down into the open, rolling pastures of Hillsbrad Foothills. There, nestled beneath the Alterac Mountains, lies Tarren Mill—a vital Forsaken hub and laboratory staging ground.

quest:494.text: Time to Strike. "Time to Strike" is a Horde reconnaissance mission that transitions scouts across the Hillsbrad Foothills border to the military hub of Tarren Mill. Delivering Deathstalker Lesh's coded signal to High Executor Darthalia marks the transition from quiet surveillance to coordinated offensive operations against the local human populace. Perched along the high ground near the border between Silverpine Forest and the Hillsbrad Foothills, Deathstalker Lesh monitors the movements of human settlers and militia in the valley below. The Deathstalkers operate as the eyes and ears of the Undercity, surveying enemy settlements before any military deployment. Rather than risk abandoning her watchpost, Lesh entrusts passing Horde travelers to relay her gathered intelligence down the road to Tarren Mill.

quest:5.text: Jitters' Growling Gut. Stranded and terrified in the ruins of Raven Hill, the paranoid vagrant Jitters is desperate for real sustenance after subsisting on weeds and insects. He begs passing adventurers to travel east to Darkshire and convince Chef Grual to prepare a hot batch of his famous Dusky Crab Cakes. Raven Hill has become a den of ravenous undead and lurking beasts, leaving the eccentric hermit Jitters trapped in hiding for weeks. Prowling through dilapidated shanties under perpetual gloom, he has survived solely on dirt-dwelling grubs and wild weeds. Starved of civilized comfort, his nerves and stomach are pushed to their absolute limits. Desperate for any reminder of safety, Jitters dreams of the seasoned patties crafted at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. He sends travelers across the haunted road to seek out Chef Grual, hoping Grual will agree to whip up a batch of Dusky Crab Cakes to quiet his violently growling gut.

quest:5042.text: Agamaggan's Strength. Agamaggan's Strength is a repeatable ritual offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. By exchanging red Blood Shards harvested across the Barrens, travelers are granted the potent physical might revered by the Razormane tribe's greatest warriors. It fuels Mangletooth's bitter hatred of the rival Bristleback quilboar. The quilboar revere the ancient boar demigod Agamaggan, whose spilled blood is said to have formed the thorny red Blood Shards scattered across the Barrens. To the quilboar, drawing upon these crystals is a sacred rite, imbuing their front-line fighters with terrifying physical might. While held captive in Camp Taurajo, the elder Razormane shaman Mangletooth is eager to impart this strength to Horde champions, claiming your foes will cower just as they do before the Razormane's most formidable champions. Mangletooth's generosity is entirely driven by spite. Captured and caged by the orcs and tauren, the old quilboar harbors a searing grudge against the rival Bristleback tribe, the enemies of his own Razormane. Since he cannot break his chains to slaughter them personally, he uses the ancient gifts of Agamaggan as currency, rewarding anyone who decimates the Bristleback tribes and strips their lands of their sacred Blood Shards.

quest:5043.text: Agamaggan's Agility. Agamaggan's Agility is a repeatable blood shard ritual offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. By offering crystalline blood shards mined from the earth of the Barrens, travelers are blessed with the unerring swiftness and accuracy of the quilboar's ancient boar god. Throughout the Barrens, strange crimson minerals known as blood shards jut from the soil, especially near quilboar encampments and colossal brambles. Quilboar tradition teaches that these crystals were formed from the spilled blood of Agamaggan, the Great Boar Ancient who perished fighting the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients. Even locked inside a wooden cage at Camp Taurajo, the elder quilboar Mangletooth retains the knowledge to channel this dormant divine power for anyone willing to supply the stones. Quilboar hunters and scouts pride themselves on ruthless accuracy and blinding quickness in the scrublands. In exchange for four blood shards, Mangletooth invokes the latent energy of the fallen demi-god, infusing the petitioner with the predatory instincts and supple grace of his people's best stalkers. Though he grunts with disdain at outsiders, Mangletooth honors his pact, weaving Agamaggan's power into a temporary mantle of agility.

quest:5044.text: Wisdom of Agamaggan. Wisdom of Agamaggan is a repeatable Horde quest offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo.
