By presenting blood shards gathered across the Barrens, spellcasters can partake in the ritualistic magic of the ancient boar god Agamaggan. Held prisoner by the Horde at Camp Taurajo, the quilboar Mangletooth trades the magical secrets of his race for crimson crystals known as blood shards. According to quilboar belief, these shards crystallized from the spilled blood of Agamaggan, the towering boar Demigod who perished in the War of the Ancients. Mangletooth claims the geomancers and shaman of his tribes rely on these shards to channel divine power into their rituals. While other offerings coax physical resilience or swiftness from the shards, the ritual of Wisdom focuses strictly on intellect and arcane capability. For the exchange of four blood shards, Mangletooth invokes the boar god's spirit on behalf of the player, wishing them cunning in their confrontations before parting with an ominous reminder of mortality.

quest:5045.text: Rising Spirit. Rising Spirit is a ritual blessing offered by the captured Razormane geomancer Mangletooth at Camp Taurajo. In exchange for blood shards wrested from his Bristleback rivals, Mangletooth channels the ancient power of Agamaggan to invigorate a champion's willpower and spiritual fortitude. Held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, the Razormane elder Mangletooth possesses deep knowledge of quilboar geomancy and ancestral magic. While other tribes may boast of raw combat ferocity, Mangletooth takes immense pride in his people's spiritual devotion to their creator, the Great Boar Agamaggan. He teaches that an unbroken spirit is what sustains a warrior when strength alone falters in battle, driving champions onward when defeat seems certain. To invoke this spiritual elevation, Mangletooth demands blood shards—crystallized fragments steeped in the ancient blood of Agamaggan that seeped into the red earth ten thousand years ago. By bringing him shards harvested from across the Barrens, particularly from his Bristleback enemies, you provide the raw spiritual conduit needed for him to weave a blessing of rising spirit that bolsters your will.

quest:5046.text: Razorhide. Razorhide is a repeatable ritual offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. By offering him blood shards infused with the life essence of the Ancient boar god Agamaggan, warriors and wanderers can gain a powerful blessing of hardened skin and resilience before heading into combat. The quilboar trace their ancestry and power directly to Agamaggan, the Great Boar who perished battling the Burning Legion thousands of years ago. His blood soaked into the soils of the Barrens, calcifying into crystalline blood shards that still thrum with ancient power. Even though the quilboar remain sworn enemies of the Horde, Mangletooth—held in a cage at Camp Taurajo—is willing to trade their sacred knowledge in exchange for these precious fragments. Natural quilboar physiology grants them thick hides and protective quills, but tribal warriors invoke Agamaggan's blessing of Razorhide to further shield themselves from enemy blades and claws. By channeling four blood shards, Mangletooth mimics this tribal rite for outsiders, magically bolstering an adventurer's defenses so their bones remain unbroken and their skin resists trauma in the wilds.

quest:5052.text: Blood Shards of Agamaggan. Mangletooth, a captive Razormane quilboar held at Camp Taurajo, reveals the sacred origin of the blood shards scattered throughout the Barrens. Imbued with the fallen demigod Agamaggan's life essence, these red minerals grant potent ancestral magic to anyone skilled enough to channel them. In exchange for the shards, the spiteful prisoner offers to share the primal boons of his god with the Horde. According to quilboar lore, the blood of the Ancient Boar God, Agamaggan, did not merely cause giant thorn mazes to erupt across the arid plains when he fell ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients. His divine blood seeped deep beneath the soil, infusing the subterranean minerals and crystallizing into blood-red stones. The quilboar revere these shards as sacred remnants of their creator, harvesting them from both mineral seams and holy grounds to serve as totems of battle and sorcery. Caged at Camp Taurajo by the tauren, Mangletooth harbors a bitter grudge against his own kind, claiming his tribe betrayed and cast him out. Deprived of his freedom and his connection to the magic of his people, he eagerly strikes a bargain with adventurers. By exchanging blood shards, Mangletooth bypasses his captivity to channel Agamaggan's power directly into Horde champions, gleefully unleashing them as an instrument of vengeance against the very quilboar who turned their backs on him. In his captivity, Mangletooth speaks reverently of the quilboar's holiest sanctuary to the south: Razorfen. To the quilboar tribes, the sprawling briars of Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs are literally formed from the fallen demigod's colossal skeleton and tusks. He warns that Razorfen Downs rests within Agamaggan's gaping maw itself—a holy threshold said to devour and crush any intruders who enter without the Boar God's favor.

quest:516.text: Beren's Peril. Beren's Peril is a Horde quest directed by Shadow Priest Allister from the Sepulcher. Agents of the Forsaken have caught wind of a hidden conclave of Scourge massing inside a secluded cave tucked into the southern Silverpine hills, aiming to strike them down before an offensive can begin. Word reached Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher that mindless servants of the Lich King were massing deep within southern Silverpine Forest. Left unchecked, these Scourge forces posed an immediate threat to Forsaken operations throughout the region. Rather than waiting for the assault to land, Allister directs scouts to take the initiative and eliminate the gathering horde inside their secluded lair before they can mobilize. Beren's Peril itself is an obscure cavern network carved into the hills south of the Dalaran-aligned settlement of Ambermill. The treacherous terrain makes the cavern easy to overlook, approached only by navigating around the southern slopes. Within its shadows dwell the Ravenclaw drudgers and guardians, entrenched remnants of the plague whose destruction helps ensure the Forsaken maintain their tenuous hold over the forest.

quest:530.text: A Husband's Revenge. A Husband's Revenge is the conclusion to a tragic tale of past betrayal carried into undeath. Raleigh Andrean, a Forsaken residing in the Undercity, charges travelers with tracking down his former friend Valdred Moray, who murdered his wife in life. When Raleigh Andrean received the engraved ring carried from Silverpine Forest, it rekindled memories of his mortal life that undeath had mostly withered away. Among those memories was a profound betrayal: his close friend, Valdred Moray, had murdered Raleigh's wife, Deliah. While the chill of the Scourge and subsequent Forsaken existence dulled Raleigh's capacity for grief and love, his thirst for retribution remained entirely intact.

quest:5321.text: The Sleeper Has Awakened. Kerlonian Evershade, a recently awakened Druid of the Claw, struggles to remain awake on his journey toward Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. Entrusted with his Horn of Awakening, travelers must shepherd the lethargic druid along the forested border, rousing him when he drifts into slumber and defending him against wild furbolgs and sinister cultists. For millennia, the Druids of the Claw slept within barrows, communing with the wild spirits across the Emerald Dream. Though the Third War demanded their awakening, shaking off centuries of hibernation does not come easily to every mind. Kerlonian Evershade set out south from Darkshore toward Ashenvale to rendezvous with Liladris Moonriver, but exhaustion overtook him shortly into his trek. Finding himself helplessly prone to sudden naps along the wilds, he relies on a brass Horn of Awakening and passing allies to keep his feet moving. The path connecting Darkshore to Ashenvale is far from tranquil. As Kerlonian meanders southward, his vulnerable state invites aggression from the surrounding wilderness. In Twilight Vale, corrupted Blackwood furbolgs stalk the roadway, while farther south into Ashenvale, members of the shadowy Dark Strand cult lurk in ambush. Escorting the groggy druid requires a vigilant watch, as Kerlonian will simply lie down to sleep wherever he stands unless forcefully roused with the horn.

quest:5643.text: Shadowguard. Shadowguard is a priestly calling issued to Darkspear troll priests who find themselves far from home in the Forsaken capital of Undercity. Aelthalyste recognizes that the young troll has matured enough for their tribe's sacred rites and sends them back to Orgrimmar. In the Valley of Spirits, the priest trainer Ur'kyo awaits to guide them into a vital tier of spiritual protection. Even in the gloom of the Undercity, the bonds of faith and tribal tradition remain strong. Forsaken priest trainer Aelthalyste observes visiting troll priests closely, noting when an initiate has grown potent enough to face their culture's trials. Rather than imposing the bleak philosophy of the Forsaken priesthood upon them, she directs the troll back across the Great Sea to the ancestral ways of their own elders. Upon arriving in Durotar, the priest makes their way to the mystic enclave of the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar. There, Ur'kyo tends to the spiritual needs and ancient rituals of the Darkspear tribe. He welcomes the returning initiate, preparing them for an essential rite of passage that bridges the priest's bond to the loa with practical spells vital for warding off harm.

quest:5644.text: Devouring Plague. Devouring Plague is a rite of passage quest for Forsaken priests journeying far from Lordaeron. Guided by the Forsaken priest trainer Miles Welsh in Thunder Bluff, the adept is directed back across the seas to Aelthalyste in the Undercity to unlock a signature manifestation of Shadow magic. While visiting Thunder Bluff, Forsaken priests who have honed their mastery over divine and shadowy disciplines are evaluated by Miles Welsh, a Forsaken priest posted among the tauren. Recognizing that an acolyte has grown sufficiently in power, Miles bids them return to the Ruins of Lordaeron rather than attempt to impart these higher mysteries himself in Kalimdor. Awaiting beneath the city ruins within the Undercity's War Quarter is Aelthalyste, one of the foremost mentors of Forsaken priesthood. She watches over the development of shadow-weaving acolytes, ensuring that the potent, draining blight known as the Devouring Plague is entrusted only to those capable of wielding its corruptive force without succumbing to it.

quest:5645.text: A Lack of Fear. A Lack of Fear is a rite-of-passage summons for dwarven priests, calling promising disciples back to the grand halls of Ironforge. High Priest Rohan awaits in the Mystic Ward to test their discipline and bestow teachings tailored to their growing resilience. Priests serving the Alliance abroad are routinely directed by their local mentors to report back to their order's senior clergy. For dwarven disciples, that guidance leads straight to High Priest Rohan in the heart of Ironforge's Mystic Ward. The summons marks a turning point where basic spiritual practice gives way to deeper, trial-tested applications of holy magic. High Priest Rohan does not simply teach liturgy; dwarven tradition views the Light as a shield and an unyielding bulwark in physical conflict. Reporting for this test acknowledges that the initiate has survived baptism through fire in the wider world and possesses the mettle required to master fear itself on the front lines.

quest:5646.text: Devouring Plague. Devouring Plague is a rite-of-passage quest for Forsaken priests who have ventured to Kalimdor to learn from the Darkspear tribe. The troll priest trainer Ur'kyo in Orgrimmar directs promising Forsaken initiates to return home to Undercity, where Aelthalyste waits to impart deeper teachings of shadow. While the orcs and tauren have little inclination toward priestly worship, the Darkspear trolls and the Forsaken share a curious theological bond within the Horde. In Orgrimmar, the troll priest trainer Ur'kyo guides those drawn to spiritual power. Yet he recognizes that Forsaken initiates must ultimately master the sinister arts unique to their own condition. In a mutual show of respect between their peoples, Ur'kyo directs wandering Forsaken back to Lordaeron to complete their training. Beneath the ruins of Lordaeron, Priestess Aelthalyste tends to the flock in the Undercity's War Quarter. Forsaken priests walk a solitary, grueling path shaped by their turn toward shadow, tempering the painful touch of the Holy Light with the devastating affliction of Shadow magic. When an initiate attains sufficient prowess, Aelthalyste gathers them close to bestow the affliction known to their kind as the Devouring Plague.

quest:5672.text: Elune's Grace. Elune's Grace is a rite of recognition offered to devout night elf priests in Darnassus. Upon proving their faith and discipline through their early journeys, priests are called before Priestess Alathea to receive deeper instruction in the divine mysteries of the Moon Goddess. Within the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, the Sisterhood of Elune guides young acolytes from their first prayers to mastery of lunar magic. Night elves do not look upon the Holy Light in the same manner as humans or dwarves; their faith is inextricably tied to the Mother Moon, Elune. When a novice priest reaches a significant milestone in their devotion, senior mentors take notice, marking the disciple as ready to shoulder greater divine power. Priestess Alathea extends this summons on behalf of the Sisterhood. She acknowledges that the acolyte's dedication has elevated them beyond the common flock, granting them access to traditions preserved across millennia. Accepting the rite seals the priest's bond to Elune, unlocking specific protective wards and lunar invocations unique to the kaldorei faith.

quest:5674.text: Elune's Grace. Elune's Grace is a rite of advancement for developing night elf priests, marking their readiness to wield divine talents unique to their people. Guided from local outposts like Dolanaar back to the sacred Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, candidates present themselves before Priestess Alathea to prove their devotion. Within the Sisterhood of Elune, a priest's journey involves more than simply mastering standard prayers of mending and smiting. As acolytes grow in experience, they reach a threshold where they are deemed ready to receive blessings granted exclusively to the kaldorei. Local mentors such as Laurna Morninglight in Dolanaar lack the authority to bestow these deeper arts, directing promising disciples back to the cultural and spiritual heart of their order. The quest directs initiates across Teldrassil to the grand Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. There, beneath the gaze of the high priesthood, Priestess Alathea evaluates whether the petitioner is truly prepared to bear the goddess's defensive mantle. Learning Elune's Grace symbolizes reaching true maturity within the priesthood, bridging the gap between raw potential and formal service to the goddess.

quest:5676.text: Arcane Feedback. Arcane Feedback is a rite of passage for Alliance priests in Stormwind City, granted by High Priestess Laurena in the Cathedral of Light. Reaching a deeper communion with faith, the priest is instructed in wards designed to counter hostile practitioners of the arcane. It represents the Church's practical defense against raw sorcery and rogue spellcasters. Within the sunlit cloisters of the Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena reminds acolytes of an enduring peril: arcane magic. While the Holy Light brings healing, warmth, and divine order, raw magical energies are volatile and often court corruption or catastrophe. To endure against warlocks, renegade sorcerers, and magical beasts, devout priests are taught that faith alone must sometimes be shaped into an active ward against ambient spells. Arcane Feedback trains the mind and spirit to punish hostile spellcasters for channeling power against the faithful. Rather than simply deflecting magical volleys, this discipline mirrors arcane energy back into its source, burning through the caster's own mana reserves while causing agony. Laurena imparts this spell to human priests stepping out into the wider world, ensuring the Cathedral's emissaries never travel defenseless against sorcery.

quest:5677.text: Arcane Feedback. Arcane Feedback is a priest quest given by High Priest Rohan in Ironforge to human acolytes visiting Khaz Modan. Rohan directs the developing priest home to the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind to receive teachings tailored specifically to the traditions of humankind. It marks a key moment of progression where young disciples begin mastering racial manifestations of their faith. When a human priest seeks advanced spiritual tutelage in the halls of the Mystic Ward, High Priest Rohan greets them with reverence but sets a boundary. While dwarven and human priests share devotion to the Holy Light, each civilization nurtures its own particular rites, disciplines, and defensive prayers. Rather than imparting Ironforge's unique secrets, Rohan sends human clergy back to their cultural roots in Elwynn, ensuring they master their people's distinct heritage. Upon returning to Stormwind City, the acolyte reports to High Priestess Laurena within the grand Cathedral of Light. Laurena is relieved to see Rohan's guidance reach the traveler, welcoming them back just as their nascent powers begin to flourish. This return paves the way for deeper initiation into the Kingdom of Stormwind's spiritual practices, preparing practitioners to wield the Holy Light against the rising threats encircling the realm.

quest:5678.text: Arcane Feedback. "Arcane Feedback" is an Alliance priest quest that directs human priests training in Darnassus back home to Stormwind. Sent by Priestess Alathea at the Temple of the Moon, the journey highlights the deep cultural rift regarding magic between the night elves and the Eastern Kingdoms. Upon returning to the Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena prepares the acolyte for deeper theological instruction. Priestess Alathea oversees visiting priests within the tranquil halls of the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. While she recognizes the formal alliance between the kaldorei and the humans of Stormwind, she harbors deep misgivings about human magical and spiritual practices. Night elf society views arcane power as inherently volatile and dangerous, shaped by ten millennia of grief following the War of the Ancients. Even divine rites from humanity that blur the lines between radiant faith and arcane mechanics make night elf clergy distinctly uneasy. Despite her hesitation, Alathea honors the bond between the Alliance races and releases the visiting acolyte to answer a recall from the Cathedral of Light. High Priestess Laurena has sent couriers across the seas to gather growing human priests for advanced training. Stepping back into Stormwind, the acolyte leaves behind the moonlit groves of Elune to embrace the grand stone sanctuaries and golden radiance of the Holy Light.

quest:5679.text: Devouring Plague. Devouring Plague is a rite of instruction offered to Forsaken priests who have proven their dedication to shadow magic. Granted by Priestess Aelthalyste in the Undercity, the teaching marks an acolyte's initiation into one of the most dreaded curses woven by the undead priesthood. In the murky cloisters of the War Quarter, Priestess Aelthalyste guides Forsaken practitioners through the grim arts of the Shadow. While living priests of other races appeal to the Holy Light or ancestral spirits for their power, the Forsaken have forged their own spiritual doctrines. Devouring Plague represents the crystallization of their philosophy: inflicting suffering upon their foes while leeching the stolen vitality back into their own decaying bodies. Aelthalyste does not offer the knowledge of the plague lightly. The spell is considered a weapon of potent malice, intended to turn the tide against the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade. When imparting the spell, Aelthalyste warns her disciples to hone their command over it through relentless practice, cautioning that far greater trials lie ahead for those who seek to master the dark arts.

quest:6284.text: Arachnophobia. Arachnophobia is a Horde bounty quest targeting Besseleth, an ancient and colossal predator haunting southern Stonetalon Mountains. Posted on a roadside notice near Windshear Crag, the bounty directs adventurers into Sishir Canyon to claim the spider matriarch's fang for Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat. Putting an end to her reign makes the mountain roads safer for night travelers. Travelers along the main thoroughfare south of Windshear Crag will spot a weathered wanted poster warning of the dangers to the west. Sishir Canyon and Webwinder Path have been completely overrun by eight-legged predators. At the heart of this webbed menace sits Besseleth, an unusually large, orange-hued spider who commands her brood and ambushes anyone daring to stray off the path after sunset. The bounty on Besseleth is offered by Maggran Earthbinder, a tauren resident of Sun Rock Retreat. Maggran has a personal score to settle with the matriarch: during a previous encounter, he was nearly killed when struck by Besseleth's massive two-foot fang. Though he managed to fight her off and limp to safety, the lingering wound serves as a constant reminder of the danger lurking in the canyon shadows. By having an adventurer claim Besseleth's Fang, Maggran hopes to secure the passes so trade and travel to Sun Rock Retreat can flourish without fear.

quest:6481.text: Earthen Arise. Deep within Boulderslide Ravine, the shaman Mor'rogal discovers a slumbering Earthen named Goggeroc sealed inside a Resonite cask. Fearing the raw destructive power an ancient being of stone could unleash upon Kalimdor, he sends a champion to shatter the cask and strike Goggeroc down before the creature can recover its full strength. While investigating the vermin infestation in Boulderslide Ravine, scouts discovered a strange relic nestled among the kobolds: a Resonite cask radiating unearthly force. Mor'rogal, a tauren shaman stationed in the Stonetalon Mountains, recognized the container for what it truly was—a prison and sanctuary housing Goggeroc, a dormant Earthen. These primordial creations of stone possess strength that outmatches mortal warriors, making the prospect of Goggeroc roaming free an existential threat to the region.

quest:6547.text: Warsong Scout Update. Warsong Scout Update is a Horde communication task connecting the outpost commanders along the borders of Ashenvale with forward scouts watching the contested forest. Carrying strategic orders from Kadrak, couriers ensure the Warsong Clan maintains tight surveillance against ambushing night elves. It highlights the tenuous, hostile grip the Horde strives to maintain over their newly claimed territory. The borderlands of Ashenvale remain a powder keg where neither side yields an inch. Horde forces under Kadrak rely heavily on dispersed Warsong scouts stationed in high-risk outposts to track night elf movements and secure contested supply lines. Because the forest itself provides natural cover to the stealthy sentinels of the Alliance, regular reports and written updates are critical to keeping isolated scouts from being cut off and overwhelmed. For the Warsong clan, every stretch of forest cleared or occupied has been paid for in blood. The scouts watch constantly for retaliatory night elf raids aiming to reclaim the woodlands. Delivering Kadrak's orders reassures the vanguard that reinforcements and coordination remain active, allowing the scouts to report back that their defensive measures are succeeding despite continuous elven resistance.

quest:731.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. Deep in the southern ruins of Darkshore, Prospector Remtravel refuses to abandon his dig site without a prize to show the Explorers' League. Despite his severe forgetfulness and an infestation of hostile troggs, he insists on uncovering a mysterious fossil before retreating. Ensuring the dwarven researcher survives his erratic search allows word of his safety to reach his assistant back in Auberdine. Remtravel's Dig lies far to the south of Darkshore, nestled among ancient ruins that were supposed to hold forgotten secrets. Instead, the dwarven excavators struck into pockets of savage troggs, driving out the workers and leaving the camp under siege. While most would flee for Auberdine immediately, Prospector Remtravel became fixated on salvaging his findings. Refusing to leave empty-handed, he wanders right into the teeth of danger to recover an elusive fossil to justify the expedition's costs to the Explorers' League.

quest:741.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. This errand delivers a strange petrified specimen recovered from the wild beaches of Darkshore to the Explorers' League outpost in Darnassus. Archaeologist Hollee refuses to abandon her distracted colleague in the field, entrusting the specimen's transport to a passing adventurer instead. The fossil's arrival in the night elven capital immediately captures the keen interest of Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker. Prospector Remtravel's excavations along the misty coast of Darkshore have unearthed a curious fossil, but digging deeper matters more to him than protocol. Archaeologist Hollee, unwilling to leave the wandering prospector alone amidst the shore's dangerous beasts and hostile cultists, remains behind to watch over him. In order to get the discovery documented, she requires an Alliance traveler to ferry the specimen up to Darnassus, where the dwarven guild maintains a scholarly delegation. Dwarves from Ironforge have crossed the Great Sea in force under the banner of the Explorers' League, eager to unearth ancient relics and lost history beneath the soil of Kalimdor. Receiving the artifact in the elven capital, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker wastes no time in marveling over Remtravel's knack for uncovering ancient treasures. While night elves view their forests as living sanctuaries, the League views the ancient lands as an expansive archaeological dig waiting to be deciphered.

quest:742.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. The Ashenvale Hunt is a summons dispatched to young Horde champions visiting Thunder Bluff, urging them north into the dense canopy of Ashenvale. Delivered by the city's heralds, the call directs travelers to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post to take part in a proving hunt. Within the serene heights of Thunder Bluff, runners keep the burgeoning Horde informed of opportunities beyond the borders of Mulgore. Bluff Runner Windstrider carries an open invitation aimed at proven adventurers looking for greater challenges. With the Horde establishing footholds deep in the ancient forest north of the Barrens, young warriors are called upon to bolster those outposts and test their survival skills in a far harsher environment. Ashenvale represents both rich resources and severe peril for the Horde. Two prominent encampments anchor the faction's presence in the territory: Splintertree Post along the main road, and a remote outpost perched upon the western coast at Zoram Strand. Arriving at Splintertree Post puts incoming recruits directly under the wing of Senani Thunderheart, a veteran outdoorswoman organizing a massive hunt designed to tame the wilderness and claim glory for the Horde.

quest:876.text: Serena Bloodfeather. This bounty task charges Horde adventurers with slaying Serena Bloodfeather, the matriarch driving harpy raids against Crossroads supply lines. Her campaign is a personal blood feud stemming from the Champion of the Horde Rexxar slaying her sister. Putting an end to Serena aims to shatter the coordination behind the harpy flock in the northern Barrens. The Witchwing harpies infesting the crags northwest of the Crossroads do not strike solely out of animalistic hunger. Their leader, Serena Bloodfeather, wages an explicit blood feud against the Horde. Years ago during the founding of Durotar, the wandering beastmaster Rexxar struck down Serena's sister, a notorious matriarch named Bloodfeather. Consumed by hatred for the nascent Horde, Serena has rallied her flock into an organized scourge intent on butchering supply trains, scouts, and merchants traveling the arid trails.

quest:878.text: Tribes at War. Tribes at War is a Horde quest offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. Trapped behind bars by the tauren, Mangletooth barters critical intelligence about quilboar incursions in exchange for the slaughter of rival Bristleback spiritual leaders. Caged in Camp Taurajo, the Razormane quilboar Mangletooth proves that captivity does not blunt old hatreds. The Barrens has long been contested between two dominant quilboar factions: the Razormane and the Bristleback. While the Horde struggles to secure its settlements and supply lines against sudden ambushes, Mangletooth offers valuable insight into who is truly tormenting Thork's outpost—provided a champion of the Horde first cuts down the Bristleback's most revered casters. Mangletooth directs adventurers north against the Bristleback's mystical core: their Water Seekers, Thornweavers, and Geomancers. Both tribes revere the earth and draw raw power from ancient magic tied to their demigod progenitor, Agamaggan. By eliminating their casters, the Horde strikes a crippling blow to Bristleback ritual strength, leaving them vulnerable to Razormane rivals and reducing pressure on nearby trails.

quest:889.text: Spirit of the Wind. Spirit of the Wind is a repeatable ritual offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. By channeling the residual power within Agamaggan's blood shards, Mangletooth infuses travelers with swiftness to outpace the vast savannas of the Barrens. In the arid sprawl of the Barrens, crossing open territory quickly can mean the difference between survival and falling to predatory beasts or wandering centaur warbands. The captive quilboar Mangletooth, imprisoned within Camp Taurajo, understands the latent power sleeping within the red crystalline blood shards scattered across the region. When handed ten of these relics, he draws upon their primeval resonance to bestow the Spirit of the Wind, granting travelers a burst of fleet-footed momentum to outrun the howling drafts of the plains. Quilboar tradition reveres Agamaggan, the Great Boar who shed his blood across central Kalimdor during the ancient War of the Ancients. Even in captivity, Mangletooth retains intimate knowledge of the wild god's rites. Channelling the god's spilled blood does not merely alter the flesh; it stirs wild vigor, allowing a runner to match the velocity of the galloping zhevra herds. Though the quilboar are bitter enemies of the Horde, Mangletooth remains willing to impart Agamaggan's boons to anyone willing to fuel his rituals with fresh shards.

quest:89.text: The Everstill Bridge. The Everstill Bridge is a rebuilding effort led by Foreman Oslow in Lakeshire to repair the town's damaged stone bridge. Progress has ground to a halt because iron meant for the project was redirected into weapons during the last orc invasion, and the replacement caravan from Stormwind was ambushed by Redridge gnolls. The stone bridge spanning Lake Everstill is the lifeblood of Lakeshire, connecting the western roads back toward Elwynn Forest with the far bank and the northern passes. During the recent orc incursions, the town was pushed to the brink. With survival hanging in the balance, Lakeshire melted down its structural iron supplies to forge munitions, blades, and plate armor to repel the Blackrock invaders, leaving the bridge incomplete and vulnerable. Foreman Oslow petitioned the House of Nobles and Stormwind for fresh construction materials to finish repairs. A supply caravan laden with iron was dispatched, but it never arrived. A warband of Redridge gnolls ambushed the convoy along the road, carting away vital iron pikes and rivets into their camps in the northern hills. Without adventurous travelers willing to reclaim the stolen hardware, the bridge project remains stalled while gnolls and orcs tighten their grip on the mountains.

quest:891.text: The Guns of Northwatch. Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun in Ratchet has had enough of his merchant vessels being blasted to splinters by the Alliance gunners at Northwatch Hold. He hires Horde champions to march down the Merchant Coast, silence the hold's artillery officers, and take the badges of their fallen infantry. Northwatch Hold looms over the southern coast of the Barrens, established as a fortified bastion for the humans of Theramore. While intended to guard Alliance interests and monitor Horde activity in Kalimdor, the soldiers within have succumbed to severe paranoia. Viewing any unfamiliar sail as hostile, their rampart batteries open fire indiscriminately, threatening peaceful merchant traffic and the privateering vessels of Ratchet. Captain Brightsun refuses to let his ships be sunk without consequence. The strike against Northwatch targets its command: Captain Fairmount and her chief cannoneers, Whessan and Smythe. Striking them down and stripping Theramore medals from the garrison's soldiers leaves the hold's artillery disarrayed, granting Ratchet's maritime operations breathing room along the Merchant Coast.

quest:898.text: Free From the Hold. Free From the Hold is an escort quest in the Barrens where Horde adventurers rescue Gilthares Firebough from human captors at Northwatch Hold. Captured after his transport was intercepted and sunk, the elf deckhand seeks a daring break out to reunite with his captain in Ratchet. Northwatch Hold stands as Theramore's military spearhead on the Barrens coast, vigilant and aggressive toward any perceived threat. That paranoia caught Gilthares Firebough in its net. His ship, running moonshine along the commercial lane between Ratchet and Booty Bay, was bombarded and sent to the ocean floor by Alliance forces. As the lone survivor plucked from the wreckage, Gilthares was thrown into Northwatch's dungeons accused of being an enemy agent conspiring against the Alliance. Despite his jailers painting him as a dangerous saboteur, Gilthares insists he is nothing more than a humble deckhand caught carrying illicit liquor. With the aid of Horde forces willing to strike at Northwatch, he makes a desperate bid for freedom, fighting his way out of the fortress and fleeing north up the shoreline to Ratchet. There, Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun welcomes the returned crewmate back into the fold of the Thalo'dan Privateers.

quest:899.text: Consumed by Hatred. Consumed by Hatred is a grim task given by Mankrik at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Tormented by the violent ambush that separated him from his wife, the grieving orc directs his agonizing uncertainty into a relentless vendetta against the Bristleback quilboar. He calls upon Horde travelers to slaughter the creatures in droves and return with a massive tally of their tusks. Standing under the harsh sun of the Crossroads, Mankrik is a warrior possessed by grief. After surviving a vicious raid by the quilboar that left him battered and his wife missing, he spends his waking hours watching the arid horizon for any sign of the pig men. His thirst for their blood remains unquenched despite the many he has personally cut down, driving him to seek help from fellow members of the Horde. Rather than seeking peace or solace, Mankrik demands trophies of raw slaughter: sixty Bristleback quilboar tusks. To him, each shattered tusk represents a measure of suffering returned upon the monsters that tore his life apart. While piles of bone cannot heal his grief or quell his desire for retribution, seeing the Bristlebacks bleed brings a fleeting, bitter satisfaction to the wounded warrior.

quest:913.text: Cry of the Thunderhawk. Cry of the Thunderhawk is the culmination of Jorn Skyseer's hunting trials in the southern Barrens. Entrusted by the elders at Camp Taurajo, a hunter must seek out a winged serpent soaring through the scrublands and bring back its wings to prove their mastery over the savanna's fiercest beasts. After proving their mettle against prowling plainstriders, prowlers, and agitated thunder lizards, hunters in the Barrens are directed toward their ultimate challenge by Jorn Skyseer. The thunderhawk is considered one of the most fierce aerial predators inhabiting the scrublands surrounding Camp Taurajo. Slaying one requires patience, sharp aim, and an awareness of the sky that few landbound predators possess. Returning with the thunderhawk's wings marks the end of a novice's tutelage under Camp Taurajo's watchful eyes. For the tauren, hunting is not mere slaughter but an ongoing spiritual walk in harmony with the Earthmother and the natural hierarchy of the wild. Besting such a proud creature shows that the hunter acts with strength, courage, and honor—virtues required before stepping out into harsher wildernesses beyond the central plains.

quest:92706.text: WANTED: Bruuz. WANTED: Bruuz is a bounty posted by Gazlowe in the goblin port of Ratchet. A massive predatory shark has taken up residence near the harbor docks, threatening maritime traffic and coastal trade until someone puts an end to it. Ratchet thrives on merchant shipping, serving as the primary neutral gateway between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. That steady stream of commerce makes the waters around the docks bustling and chaotic, but recently it has drawn a far more dangerous visitor. A gargantuan shark, dubbed 'Bruuz' by the frightened dockworkers, has begun prowling the bay. Rather than remaining in deep water, the beast aggressively targets small skiffs, local sailors, and offloading cargo, disrupting port operations. Gazlowe cannot afford to have vessels avoiding his port out of fear of getting mauled by sea life. So he has posted a public bounty notice calling on all anglers and promising a hefty reward. To claim it, a hunter must slay Bruuz and haul back the predator's dorsal fin as proof of the deed.

quest:93.text: Dusky Crab Cakes. Chef Grual of Darkshire's Scarlet Raven Tavern has a secret behind his famous Dusky Crab Cakes: they contain no crab at all. Tasked with aiding the famished and nervous Jitters, adventurers are sent to harvest spider legs from the deadly arachnids roaming northern Duskwood to prepare the town's beloved snack. Duskwood has long suffered from isolation, dark magic, and severed supply routes, forcing the locals of Darkshire to adapt their cuisine. Chef Grual, the resident cook at the Scarlet Raven Tavern, solved his meat shortages by inventing the Dusky Crab Cake. Despite the name suggesting seafood from distant shores, Grual readily admits that the dish's distinctively tangy flavor comes entirely from the gooey legs of local giant spiders. To fulfill the order, Grual directs hunters north toward the foothills and riverbanks where Venom Web Spiders spin their snares. In a gloomy forest crawling with undead and feral beasts, harvesting fresh spider meat is hazardous work, yet it remains one of the few readily available protein sources in the blighted woods. Grual fries the seasoned arachnid limbs on a hot skillet until they skitter to a crisp.

quest:94.text: A Watchful Eye. A Watchful Eye is an Alliance quest issued by the wizard Theocritus from the Tower of Azora in Elwynn Forest. Having established a basic scrying link against his rival Morganth, Theocritus directs adventurers east into Redridge Mountains to plant an enchanted focus upon an ancient lion statue watching the Tower of Ilgalar. From his tower in eastern Elwynn Forest, the mage Theocritus maintains a vigilant watch over dark spellcraft brewing in the nearby hills. His chief nemesis is Morganth, a vicious sorcerer of formidable power who has claimed the Tower of Ilgalar in the crags of Redridge Mountains. Seeking to uncover Morganth's sinister ambitions before they spill across the border, Theocritus developed the Eye of Azora to surveil the rogue wizard from a distance. While visual scrying affords some information, it is not enough to divine Morganth's deeper schemes. Theocritus entrusts travelers with the Glyph of Azora, commanding them to trek to the shadow of the Tower of Ilgalar. There, keeping a lonely watch for decades, stands an Old Lion Statue. Setting the glyph into a worn depression at the statue's base awakens an arcane conduit, linking the stone back to Azora and allowing Theocritus to delve straight into his rival's mind.

quest:942.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. This quest bridges an excavation mystery from Darkshore across the Great Sea to the Wetlands. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker entrusts you with a strange Kalimdor fossil, directing you to Archaeologist Flagongut in Menethil Harbor to unlock its secrets. While examining the strange fossil uncovered in Darkshore, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker notices a striking resemblance to a relic shown at an Explorers' League conference back in Ironforge. That earlier piece was presented by Archaeologist Flagongut, who was convinced that such fossils held latent powers waiting to be unlocked. Greywhisker believes Flagongut is the only dwarf capable of discerning what makes this Kalimdor find so extraordinary. Carrying the mysterious relic means undertaking a long journey out of Kalimdor to the Eastern Kingdoms. Flagongut was last seen waiting for an armed escort to the Whelgar Excavation Site while lodging at the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Delivering the fossil into his hands marks the turning point where a local Darkshore survey ties into a continent-spanning archaeological inquiry.

quest:951.text: Mathystra Relics. This quest sends Alliance adventurers north along the coast of Darkshore to sift through the overgrown Ruins of Mathystra. Onu, an Ancient of Lore rooted in the Grove of the Ancients, seeks these ancient kaldorei artifacts to understand how the Twilight's Hammer cult is manipulating night elven sorcery for their sinister rites. To counteract this dark endeavor, Onu directs heroes to the Ruins of Mathystra, located along the northeastern shores of Darkshore. Long ago, Mathystra was a shining bastion of highborne civilization before it shattered during the Sundering. Though the city has collapsed into rubble, weeds, and naga infestation, powerful remnants of its original arcane and spiritual enchantments linger in shattered urns and ancient relics scattered across the stone foundations.

quest:970.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. This quest marks a critical turn in the investigation of the sinister Cult of the Dark Strand, shifting the pursuit from the ruined Tower of Althalaxx in Darkshore across the border to Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. Delgren the Purifier dispatches adventurers into nearby cultist camps to secure a potent Glowing Soul Gem. Unlocking this artifact reveals the grim sorcery that fuels the cult's influence over the northern forests. After uncovering the ominous activities around the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore, reports led directly south into Ashenvale to Delgren the Purifier. Stationed at Maestra's Post, Delgren has long contended with the Cult of the Dark Strand encroaching on the ancient elven woods. Recognizing that the cult's threat spans across both territories, Delgren resolves to strike at the heart of their vile sorcery. Northeast of Maestra's Post lies the ruins of Ordil'Aran, now overrun by fanatical Dark Strand cultists. Delgren identifies that their operatives carry glowing soul gems—dark vessels enchanted with sinister magic that sustain the cult's power. By hunting down the cultists among the ruins and reclaiming one of these gems, Delgren intends to shatter their enchantment and expose the true source behind their malevolent rite.

quest:972.text: Water Sapta. Water Sapta is a transitional task bestowed upon young Horde shaman by Islen Waterseer along the coast of the Barrens. Imbued with a ritual brew, the shaman is sent across the Great Sea to the blighted lands of Silverpine Forest to face a corrupted spring. In the elemental traditions of the Horde's shaman, a sapta is an alchemical draught crafted to attune the senses directly to the spirits of the world. While common eyes perceive only tranquil streams or stagnant ponds, drinking a sapta pierces the veil of the physical plane, revealing the elemental beings dwelling within the current. Having demonstrated their dedication to the spirits, the shaman receives the concoction directly from Islen Waterseer, a hermit dwelling along the desolate shores south of Ratchet. Rather than testing the sapta in the arid valleys of Kalimdor, Islen commands the initiate to journey far across the Great Sea to the shadowy, forsaken woods of Silverpine Forest to confront an elemental corruption poisoning Lordaeron's streams.

quest:98362.text: To Thunder Bluff. To Thunder Bluff marks the triumphant return of a young tauren druid from their communion with the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. Having earned the favor of the Great Cat Spirit, the initiate returns to Turak Runetotem on the Elder Rise to master the art of feline shapeshifting. After proving their insight and worth before Dendrite Starblaze and the Great Cat Spirit in the sacred groves of Moonglade, a young druid must carry the spirit's blessings back to Mulgore. The communion with such primal powers represents a pivotal milestone in a druid's training, bridging ancient night elven teachings with the tauren's own earthen heritage. Awaiting your return high atop the Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff is Turak Runetotem. While Dendrite facilitated communion with the spirit itself, it falls to Turak to guide the physical transformation. With the blessing of the Great Cat Spirit acknowledged, the elder trainer imparts the sacred knowledge required to adopt the swift, predatory shape of the cat.

quest:98397.text: To Darnassus. To Darnassus is the culmination of a night elf druid's journey to commune with the Great Cat Spirit. After proving yourself to Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade, you are sent back to the Cenarion Enclave to master the art of shifting into cat form. Having commune with the Great Cat Spirit through the guidance of Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade, an aspiring night elf druid must return to Teldrassil. Starblaze acknowledges that you have proven yourself a worthy student and directs you back to your primary instructor, Mathrengyl Bearwalker, waiting beneath the boughs of the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. Upon arriving in Darnassus, Mathrengyl Bearwalker acknowledges that you have absorbed the wisdom of the Great Cat Spirit. In his eyes, every generation of druids faces a trial shaped by this ancient entity, which is as playful as it is deadly. With your connection established and your spirit prepared, Mathrengyl imparts the final rites necessary to shift into the graceful form of the cat.

quest:986.text: A Lost Master. A Lost Master tasks an Alliance adventurer with gathering materials to aid in the search for Volcor, a night elf lost in the wilderness of Darkshore. Terenthis in Auberdine offers to weave an enchanted camouflage cloak to protect the rescuer, requiring pelts from the coast's fiercest moonstalkers. While tracking threats along the coast of Darkshore, Terenthis in Auberdine becomes concerned for the fate of Volcor and his companion, Grimclaw. Venturing deep into the southern reaches of the region is notoriously dangerous due to aggressive predators and corrupted wildlife. Rather than sending a scout unprotected, Terenthis devises a plan to craft a protective cloak imbued with wild illusions. To weave a cloak capable of confounding Darkshore's beasts, standard hides are insufficient. Terenthis requires fine moonstalker pelts taken specifically from mature moonstalker sires or matriarchs. These formidable great cats prowl the woodlands south of Auberdine near the Wildbend River and extend toward the forested border of Ashenvale. The finished garment uses moonstalker fur and nature enchantments to let the wearer pass unhindered through hostile territory while searching for Volcor. However, Terenthis warns that the illusion is delicate: engaging in strenuous activity or combat breaks the enchantment, leaving the searcher exposed.

quest:993.text: A Lost Master. Having gathered fine moonstalker pelts, you carry the completed Enchanted Moonstalker Cloak into the wilds of Darkshore to find the missing night elf, Volcor. Guided by his loyal white bear Grimclaw, you must track down the wounded scout before hostile furbolgs finish him off. After Terenthis in Auberdine weaves the Enchanted Moonstalker Cloak, the search for the missing scout Volcor begins in earnest. His bear companion, Grimclaw, has returned to the road south of the settlement, standing watch for any ally sent by Terenthis. By offering a familiar greeting to the loyal beast, travelers are led directly off the beaten track toward the cave where Volcor lies in hiding.

quest:995.text: Escape Through Stealth. Escape Through Stealth is an Alliance escort quest set in Darkshore. After locating the trapped night elf scout Volcor deep within a furbolg den, the player helps guide him safely past hostile beasts to freedom before reporting back to Terenthis in Auberdine. Volcor, an operative sent into the depths of Darkshore to investigate the region's mounting threats, ended up cornered inside a furbolg cave. Outnumbered and cut off from the main roads, he relies on a passing ally to coordinate an exit before the hostile furbolgs realize he is slipping away. Rather than attempting a suicidal frontal charge, Volcor chooses caution. Relying on shadows and deliberate maneuvering, he slips past the corrupted denizens of the cavern. Knowing that speed and quiet are paramount, Volcor separates from his rescuer once outside the mouth of the cave, racing ahead on foot while instructing his savior to meet him at the settlement of Auberdine. Upon returning to Auberdine, the player delivers news of the rescue to Terenthis, a night elf leader coordinating efforts to protect the troubled coastline. Terenthis views Volcor's safe return as proof that the encroaching darkness throughout Darkshore and the wilderness beyond can be resisted with discipline and teamwork.
